translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 229.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀四十五】 起昭陽大淵獻十一月，盡閼逢困敦正月，不滿一年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 45] Beginning in the eleventh month of the sexagenary cycle year Zhaoyang Dayuanxian, ending in the first month of Efeng Kundun—less than one full year.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 45] This record runs from the eleventh month of one cycle year to the first month of the next—less than a full year.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝四建中四年（

translations.literal: The fourth year of Jianzhong of Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial Sagely Cultural Emperor (
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianzhong of Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial and Sagely Cultural Emperor (

sentences.zh: 癸亥，公元七八三年）

translations.literal: Guihai, AD 783)
translations.idiomatic: Guihai, AD 783)

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁亥，以隴州為奉義軍，擢皋為節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dinghai, Long Prefecture was made the Fengyi Army [command], and Gao was promoted to military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day dinghai, Long Prefecture was designated the Fengyi Army district and Gao was appointed its military governor.

sentences.zh: 泚又使中使劉海廣許皋鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: Ci again sent the palace envoy Liu Haiguang to promise Gao the post of Fengxiang military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci also sent the court envoy Liu Haiguang to offer Gao the Fengxiang military governorship.

sentences.zh: 皋斬之。

translations.literal: Gao executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao had him executed.

sentences.zh: 靈武留後杜希全、鹽州刺史戴休顏、夏州刺史時常春會渭北節度使李建徽，合兵萬人入援，將至奉天，上召將相議道所從出。

translations.literal: Lingwu acting prefect Du Xiquan, Yanzhou prefect Dai Xiuyan, and Xiazhou prefect Shi Changchun joined Weibei military governor Li Jianhui; together they mustered ten thousand men to march to the rescue. As they were about to reach Fengtian, the emperor summoned generals and ministers to discuss which route they should take.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiquan, acting prefect of Lingwu, Dai Xiuyan, prefect of Yan, and Shi Changchun, prefect of Xia, joined Li Jianhui, military governor of Weibei, and together led ten thousand troops to relieve the siege. When they were nearing Fengtian, the emperor called his generals and ministers together to decide which route the relief force should take.

sentences.zh: 關播、渾瑊曰：「漠谷道險狹，恐為賊所邀。

translations.literal: Guan Bo and Hun Jian said: "The Mogu route is narrow and perilous; we fear the rebels may ambush us there.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bo and Hun Jian said, "The Mogu pass is narrow and dangerous—the rebels may well ambush us there.

sentences.zh: 不若自乾陵北過，附柏城而行，營於城東北雞子堆，與城中掎角相應，且分賊勢。」

translations.literal: It would be better to pass north of Qianling, follow along the cypress city, and encamp at Jizidui northeast of the city, coordinating with the city in pincer fashion and also dividing the rebel strength."
translations.idiomatic: Better to march north of Qianling, keep to the cypress rampart road, and camp at Jizidui northeast of the city. That way we can support Fengtian in a pincer and split the rebel forces."

sentences.zh: 盧杞曰：「漠谷路近，若為賊所邀，則城中出兵應接可也。

translations.literal: Lu Qi said: "The Mogu road is shorter; if they are ambushed, troops from the city can sally out to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi said, "The Mogu route is shorter. If the rebels intercept them there, the city can send troops out to link up.

sentences.zh: 倘出乾陵，恐驚陵寢。」

translations.literal: If they go by way of Qianling, I fear we may disturb the imperial tombs."
translations.idiomatic: But if they pass Qianling, we may disturb the imperial tombs."

sentences.zh: 瑊曰：「自泚圍城，斬乾陵松柏，以夜繼晝，其驚多矣。

translations.literal: Jian said: "Since Ci besieged the city, he has cut down the pines and cypresses of Qianling, working night and day—how much disturbance has there already been!
translations.idiomatic: Jian replied, "Since Zhu Ci laid siege, he has been felling the pines and cypresses of Qianling day and night—how much more disturbance could there be?

sentences.zh: 今城中危急，諸道救兵未至，惟希全等來，所繫非輕，若得營據要地，則泚可破也。」

translations.literal: Now the city is in grave peril; relief armies from the circuits have not yet arrived—only Xiquan and the others are coming, and what hangs on them is no small matter. If they can encamp at a strategic point, Ci can be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: The city is in desperate straits. No relief armies from the provinces have arrived yet—only Xiquan and his men are coming, and everything depends on them. If they can seize a strong position, Zhu Ci can be broken."

sentences.zh: 杞曰：「陛下行師，豈比逆賊！

translations.literal: Qi said: "When Your Majesty moves troops, how can that be compared with rebels!
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "When Your Majesty sends an army, how can that be compared with rebel bandits!

sentences.zh: 若令希全等過之，是自驚陵寢。」

translations.literal: If Xiquan and the others are made to pass there, that would be to disturb the tombs ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: If you order Xiquan and his men to march past the tombs, we ourselves will be the ones disturbing the imperial resting place."

sentences.zh: 上乃命希全等自漠谷進。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Xiquan and the others to advance by way of Mogu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Xiquan and his force to advance through Mogu.

sentences.zh: 丙子，希全等軍至漠谷，果為賊所邀，乘高以大弩、巨石擊之，死傷甚眾。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Xiquan's army reached Mogu and was indeed ambushed by the rebels, who from high ground struck them with great crossbows and boulders; casualties were very heavy.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingzi, Xiquan's army reached Mogu and was ambushed as predicted. The rebels rained down boulders and bolts from the heights, and casualties were heavy.

sentences.zh: 城中出兵應接，為賊所敗。

translations.literal: Troops sallied from the city to meet them but were defeated by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Troops sallied from the city to link up with them but were beaten back by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 是夕，四軍潰，退保邠州。

translations.literal: That evening the four armies broke and fell back to defend Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That night all four armies broke and retreated to Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 泚閱其輜重於城下，從官相視失色。

translations.literal: Ci reviewed their baggage train below the city walls; the attendants looked at one another, their faces drained of color.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci paraded the captured baggage train beneath the walls. The officials who accompanied the emperor looked at one another, their faces ashen.

sentences.zh: 休顏，夏州人也。

translations.literal: Xiuyan was a native of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyan was a native of Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 泚攻城益急，穿塹環之。

translations.literal: Ci pressed the siege ever harder, digging trenches to ring the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci pressed the siege harder still, digging trenches to ring the city.

sentences.zh: 泚移帳於乾陵，下視城中，動靜皆見之。

translations.literal: Ci moved his headquarters to Qianling, looking down on the city so that every movement within was visible.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci moved his headquarters to Qianling, where he could look down on the city and see everything that moved within it.

sentences.zh: 時遣使環城招誘士民，笑其不識天命。

translations.literal: He constantly sent envoys around the city to entice soldiers and civilians, mocking them for not recognizing Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: He kept sending envoys around the walls to entice soldiers and civilians, mocking them for failing to recognize Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 神策河北行營節度使李晟疾愈，聞上幸奉天，帥眾將奔命。

translations.literal: Li Sheng, military governor of the Shence Hebei campaign army, having recovered from illness, heard that the emperor had gone to Fengtian and was about to lead his troops to rush to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng, military governor of the Shence Hebei campaign army, had recovered from illness. When he learned that the emperor had fled to Fengtian, he prepared to march to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 張孝忠迫於朱滔、王武俊，倚晟為援，不欲晟行，數沮止之。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaozhong, pressed by Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun, relied on Sheng as his support and did not want Sheng to leave; he repeatedly obstructed and dissuaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaozhong, hard pressed by Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun, depended on Li Sheng for support and did not want him to leave. He repeatedly blocked and dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 晟乃留其子憑，使娶孝忠女為婦，又解玉帶賂孝忠親信，使說之。

translations.literal: Sheng therefore left his son Ping, had him marry Xiaozhong's daughter, and also removed his jade belt to bribe Xiaozhong's close associates, having them persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng left his son Ping behind to marry Zhang Xiaozhong's daughter, and gave his jade belt to Xiaozhong's intimates to win them over on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 孝忠乃聽晟西歸，遣大將楊榮國將銳兵六百與晟俱。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong then allowed Sheng to return west and sent the great general Yang Rongguo with six hundred crack troops to go with Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaozhong finally let Li Sheng march west, and sent his general Yang Rongguo with six hundred elite troops to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 晟引兵出飛狐道，晝夜兼行，至代州。

translations.literal: Sheng led his troops out by the Feihu route, marching day and night without rest, and reached Dai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng led his men out through the Feihu pass, marching day and night without rest until he reached Dai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，加晟神策行營節度使。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Sheng was given the additional title of Shence campaign military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou, Li Sheng was appointed Shence campaign military governor.

sentences.zh: 王武俊、馬寔攻趙州不克。

translations.literal: Wang Wujun and Ma Sui attacked Zhao Prefecture but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun and Ma Sui attacked Zhao Prefecture without success.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，寔歸瀛州，武俊送之五里，犒贈甚厚。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Sui returned to Ying Prefecture; Wujun escorted him five li and gave him lavish gifts and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinsi, Ma Sui returned to Ying Prefecture. Wang Wujun escorted him five li and sent him off with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 武俊亦歸恆州。

translations.literal: Wujun also returned to Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun then returned to Heng Prefecture as well.

sentences.zh: 上之出幸奉天也，陝虢觀察使姚明易文以軍事委都防禦副使張勸，去詣行在。

translations.literal: When the emperor departed for Fengtian, Yao Mingyi, observation commissioner of Shan-Guo, entrusted military affairs to the deputy metropolitan defense commissioner Zhang Quan and went to join the imperial presence.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled to Fengtian, Yao Mingyi, observation commissioner of Shan and Guo, left military affairs in the hands of his deputy defense commissioner Zhang Quan and went to join the emperor.

sentences.zh: 勸募兵得數萬人。

translations.literal: Quan raised troops and obtained several tens of thousands of men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quan raised troops and mustered tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以勸為陝虢節度使。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Quan was made military governor of Shan-Guo.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiashen, Zhang Quan was appointed military governor of Shan and Guo.

sentences.zh: 朱泚攻圍奉天經月，城中資糧俱盡。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci had besieged Fengtian for a month; within the city supplies of provisions were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci had besieged Fengtian for a month, and the city's stores of food were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 上嘗遣健步出城覘賊，其人懇以苦寒為辭，跪奏乞一襦褲誇。

translations.literal: The emperor once sent a swift runner out of the city to reconnoiter the rebels; the man earnestly pleaded the bitter cold as his excuse, knelt and memorialized, begging for a single padded jacket and trousers to boast of.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once sent a swift runner out to scout the rebel lines. The man pleaded bitter cold, knelt before the throne, and begged for a single padded jacket and trousers.

sentences.zh: 上為之尋求不獲，竟憫默而遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor searched for him but could not find any; in the end he dismissed him in silent compassion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had his attendants search but none could be found. In the end he sent the man away in sorrowful silence.

sentences.zh: 時供御才有糲米二斛，每伺賊之休息，夜，縋人於城外，采蕪菁根而進之。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial kitchen had only two hu of coarse millet; whenever the rebels rested, at night men were lowered by rope outside the walls to gather turnip roots and bring them in.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial kitchen had only two hu of coarse millet left. Whenever the rebels eased their assault, men were lowered by rope at night to gather turnip roots outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 上召公卿將吏謂曰：「朕以不德，自陷危亡，固其宜也。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the high ministers, generals, and officials and said: "Through my lack of virtue I have brought myself to peril and ruin—this is only fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned his ministers, generals, and officials and said, "Through my own want of virtue I have brought us to the brink of ruin—that is only fitting.

sentences.zh: 公輩無罪，宜早降，以救室家。」

translations.literal: You are without guilt; you should surrender early to save your households."
translations.idiomatic: You are innocent. You should surrender soon and save your families."

sentences.zh: 群臣皆頓首流涕，期盡死力，故將士雖困急而銳氣不衰。

translations.literal: All the ministers bowed their heads and wept, pledging to exert themselves to the death; therefore though the officers and soldiers were in desperate straits, their fighting spirit did not flag.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all prostrated themselves, weeping, and pledged to fight to the death. Though the soldiers were starving and exhausted, their fighting spirit never faltered.

sentences.zh: 上之幸奉天也，糧料使崔縱勸李懷光令入援，懷光從之。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Fengtian, the grain commissioner Cui Zong urged Li Huaiguang to march in relief, and Huaiguang followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled to Fengtian, the grain commissioner Cui Zong persuaded Li Huaiguang to march to the rescue, and Huaiguang agreed.

sentences.zh: 縱悉斂軍資與懷光皆來。

translations.literal: Zong gathered all military supplies and came with Huaiguang.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zong gathered all military supplies and marched with Huaiguang.

sentences.zh: 懷光晝夜倍道，至河中，力疲，休兵三日。

translations.literal: Huaiguang marched day and night by forced marches; reaching Hezhong, his men exhausted, he rested the army three days.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang forced the march day and night. When he reached Hezhong his men were exhausted, and he rested the army for three days.

sentences.zh: 河中尹李齊運傾力犒宴，軍士尚欲遷延。

translations.literal: Li Qiyun, prefect of Hezhong, exerted all his strength in feasting and rewarding them, yet the soldiers still wished to delay.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiyun, prefect of Hezhong, lavished feasts and rewards on the army, yet the soldiers still wanted to linger.

sentences.zh: 崔縱先輦貨財渡河，謂眾曰：「至河西，悉以分賜。」

translations.literal: Cui Zong first had goods and wealth carted across the river and said to the troops: "When we reach the west of the river, all will be distributed as rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zong had goods and wealth ferried across the river ahead of the army and told the troops, "When we reach the west bank, everything will be divided among you.

sentences.zh: 眾利之，西屯蒲城，有眾五萬。

translations.literal: The troops were enticed by this; they encamped west at Pucheng, numbering fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The promise stirred them. They crossed west and encamped at Pucheng with fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 齊運，惲之孫也。

translations.literal: Qiyun was a grandson of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyun was a grandson of Li Yun.

sentences.zh: 李晟行且收兵，亦自蒲津濟，軍於東渭橋。

translations.literal: Li Sheng, marching and gathering troops as he went, also crossed at Pujin and encamped at the Eastern Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng marched west, gathering troops along the way, crossed at Pujin, and encamped at the Eastern Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 其始有卒四千，晟善於撫御，與士卒同甘苦，人樂從之，旬月間至萬餘人。

translations.literal: At first he had four thousand soldiers; Sheng was skilled in comforting and controlling them, sharing hardship and comfort with the troops, and men were glad to follow him—in the space of ten days and a month he reached more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He began with four thousand men. Li Sheng was a master at winning soldiers' loyalty, sharing their hardships and comforts alike, and men flocked to his banner. Within a month his force had grown to more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 神策兵馬使尚可孤討李希烈，將三千人在襄陽，自武關入援，軍於七盤，敗泚將仇敬，遂取藍田。

translations.literal: Shang Ke'gu, Shence horse-and-army commissioner campaigning against Li Xilie, commanded three thousand men at Xiangyang; entering by Wuguan to relieve the siege, he encamped at Qipan, defeated Ci's general Qiu Jing, and then took Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Ke'gu, a Shence cavalry commissioner campaigning against Li Xilie, commanded three thousand men at Xiangyang. He entered through Wuguan to relieve the siege, encamped at Qipan, defeated Zhu Ci's general Qiu Jing, and seized Lantian.

sentences.zh: 可孤，宇文部之別種也。

translations.literal: Ke'gu was of a separate branch of the Yuwen tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Ke'gu was of a collateral branch of the Yuwen people.

sentences.zh: 鎮國軍副使駱元光，其先安息人，駱奉先養以為子，將兵守潼關近十年，為眾所服。

translations.literal: Luo Yuanguang, deputy commissioner of the Zhenguo Army, was by ancestry a man of Parthia; Luo Fengxian had adopted him as a son. He had commanded troops guarding Tong Pass for nearly ten years and was respected by all.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yuanguang, deputy commissioner of the Zhenguo Army, was descended from Parthians. Luo Fengxian had adopted him as a son. He had held Tong Pass with his troops for nearly ten years and was deeply respected by his men.

sentences.zh: 朱泚遣其將何望之襲華州，刺史董晉棄州走行在。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci sent his general He Wangzhi to strike at Hua Prefecture; the prefect Dong Jin abandoned the prefecture and fled to the imperial presence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci sent his general He Wangzhi to seize Hua Prefecture. The prefect Dong Jin abandoned the city and fled to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 望之據其城，將聚兵以絕東道。

translations.literal: Wangzhi seized the city and was about to gather troops to cut off the eastern route.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi occupied the city and prepared to mass troops to sever the eastern supply route.

sentences.zh: 元光引關下兵襲望之，走還長安。

translations.literal: Yuanguang led troops from below the Pass to attack Wangzhi, who fled back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanguang led his troops from below the Pass against Wangzhi, who fled back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 元光遂軍華州，召募士卒，數日，得萬餘人。

translations.literal: Yuanguang then encamped at Hua Prefecture, recruited soldiers, and within several days obtained more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanguang then encamped at Hua Prefecture, raised troops, and within days had more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 泚數遣兵攻元光，元光皆擊卻之，賊由是不能東出。

translations.literal: Ci repeatedly sent troops to attack Yuanguang, but Yuanguang beat them all back; because of this the rebels could not advance eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci sent repeated attacks against Yuanguang, but Yuanguang drove them all back. The rebels were unable to push eastward.

sentences.zh: 上即以元光為鎮國軍節度使，元光乃將兵二千西屯昭應。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately made Yuanguang military governor of the Zhenguo Army; Yuanguang then led two thousand troops west to encamp at Zhaoying.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promptly appointed Yuanguang military governor of the Zhenguo Army. Yuanguang then led two thousand men west to encamp at Zhaoying.

sentences.zh: 馬燧遣其行軍司馬王權及其子匯將兵五千人入援，屯中渭橋。

translations.literal: Ma Sui sent his campaign chief of staff Wang Quan and his son Hui with five thousand troops to enter as relief, encamping at the Central Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui sent his campaign chief of staff Wang Quan and his son Hui with five thousand troops to relieve the siege. They encamped at the Central Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 於是泚黨所據惟長安而已，援軍游騎時至望春樓下。

translations.literal: At this point the only place held by Ci's faction was Chang'an alone; relief-army scouting horsemen sometimes reached below Wangchun Tower.
translations.idiomatic: By now Zhu Ci's followers held only Chang'an itself. Scouting parties from the relief armies sometimes reached as far as Wangchun Tower.

sentences.zh: 李忠臣等屢出兵皆敗，求救於泚，泚恐民間乘弊抄之，所遣兵皆晝伏夜行。

translations.literal: Li Zhongchen and others repeatedly sent out troops and were defeated each time; they begged Ci for rescue. Ci feared the populace would take advantage to raid them, so the troops he sent all traveled by day hidden and by night on the march.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchen and his allies sent out troops again and again only to be defeated. They begged Zhu Ci for help. Zhu Ci feared that civilians would take advantage to raid his messengers, so he sent his troops out only at night, hiding by day.

sentences.zh: 泚內以長安為憂，乃急攻奉天，使僧法堅造雲梯，高廣各數丈，裹以兕革，下施巨輪，上容壯士五百人。

translations.literal: Within, Ci was anxious about Chang'an; he therefore pressed the attack on Fengtian fiercely, having the monk Fajian build siege towers: height and breadth each several zhang, wrapped in rhinoceros hide, with great wheels below, able to hold five hundred stalwart men above.
translations.idiomatic: Anxious about Chang'an, Zhu Ci redoubled his assault on Fengtian. He had the monk Fajian build siege towers several zhang high and wide, sheathed in rhinoceros hide, mounted on great wheels below, each able to carry five hundred men aloft.

sentences.zh: 城中望之忷懼。

translations.literal: Looking at them from within the city, all were fearful and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Those within the city looked on in dread.

sentences.zh: 上以問群臣，渾瑊、侯仲莊對曰：「臣觀雲梯勢甚重，重則易陷。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned the ministers about it; Hun Jian and Hou Zhongzhuang replied: "We observe that the siege towers' momentum is very heavy; when heavy, they are easy to sink.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers what to do. Hun Jian and Hou Zhongzhuang replied, "Those towers are enormously heavy—too heavy to move easily.

sentences.zh: 臣請迎其所來鑿地道，積薪蓄火以待之。」

translations.literal: We ask to meet them where they come, dig a tunnel, pile firewood and store fire to await them."
translations.idiomatic: Let us dig a tunnel where they will approach, pile fuel, and wait with fire ready."

sentences.zh: 神武軍使韓澄曰：「雲梯小伎，不足上勞聖慮，臣請御之。」

translations.literal: Han Cheng, commissioner of the Shenwu Army, said: "Siege towers are a petty device—not worth troubling Your Sacred concern; I ask to deal with them myself."
translations.idiomatic: Han Cheng, commissioner of the Shenwu Army, said, "Siege towers are a petty trick—not worth troubling Your Majesty. Let me handle them."

sentences.zh: 乃度梯之所傃，廣城東北隅三十步，多儲膏油松脂薪葦於其上。

translations.literal: He then estimated where the towers would lean, widened the northeast corner of the city thirty paces, and stored much grease, pine resin, firewood, and reeds there.
translations.idiomatic: He calculated where the towers would bear, widened the northeast corner of the wall by thirty paces, and stockpiled grease, pine resin, firewood, and reeds there.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，泚盛兵鼓噪攻南城，韓游瑰曰：「此欲分吾力也。」

translations.literal: On dinghai, Ci massed troops with drums and shouts to attack the southern wall; Han Yougui said: "This is meant to divide our strength."
translations.idiomatic: On the day dinghai, Zhu Ci massed his troops with drums and war cries against the southern wall. Han Yougui said, "He means to divide our strength."

sentences.zh: 乃引兵嚴備東北。

translations.literal: He then led troops to make strict preparations in the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men to strengthen the northeast instead.

sentences.zh: 戊子，北風甚迅，泚推雲梯，上施濕氈，懸水囊，載壯士攻城，翼以轒轀，置人其下，抱薪負土填塹而前，矢石火炬所不能傷。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the north wind blew very fiercely; Ci pushed forward the siege towers, hung wet felt above, suspended water bags, loaded stalwart men to assault the walls, flanked them with catapults, and placed men below carrying firewood and bearing earth to fill the moat as they advanced—arrows, stones, and torches could not harm them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuzi a fierce north wind blew. Zhu Ci pushed the siege towers forward, draped them in wet felt, hung water bags from them, and loaded them with assault troops. Catapults flanked the towers while men below carried firewood and earth to fill the moat. Arrows, stones, and fire could not touch them.

sentences.zh: 賊並兵攻城東北隅，矢石如雨，城中死傷者不可勝數。

translations.literal: The rebels combined their forces to attack the northeast corner of the city; arrows and stones fell like rain; within the city the dead and wounded were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels massed against the northeast corner. Arrows and stones fell like rain, and the dead and wounded within the city were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 賊已有登城者，上與渾瑊對泣，群臣惟仰首祝天。

translations.literal: The rebels already had men who had climbed the wall; the emperor and Hun Jian wept face to face; the ministers could only raise their heads and pray to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels had already gained the wall. The emperor and Hun Jian wept in each other's arms while the ministers could only raise their eyes to Heaven and pray.

sentences.zh: 上以無名告身自御史大夫、實食五百戶以下千餘通授瑊，使募敢死士御之，仍賜御筆，使視其功之在小書名給之，告身不足則書其身，且曰：「今便與卿別。」

translations.literal: The emperor took more than a thousand blank commissions from Grand Censor on down, with stipends of five hundred households and below, and gave them to Jian, ordering him to recruit dare-to-die men to resist; he also bestowed his imperial brush, telling him to note achievements in small script and award them on the spot—if commissions ran out, to write names on their bodies—and said: "Today I take leave of you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Hun Jian more than a thousand blank commissions—from Grand Censor down to stipends of five hundred households—and told him to recruit dare-to-die men to hold the line. He also gave him his own brush and told him to note each man's deeds in small script and award commissions on the spot; if the blanks ran out, to write names on the men's bodies. He said, "This may be our farewell."

sentences.zh: 瑊俯伏流涕，上拊其背，歔欷不自勝。

translations.literal: Jian prostrated himself weeping; the emperor patted his back, sobbing uncontrollably.
translations.idiomatic: Jian prostrated himself, weeping. The emperor patted his back, overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 時士卒凍餒，又逐甲冑，瑊扶諭，激以忠義，皆鼓噪力戰。

translations.literal: At the time the soldiers were frozen and starving, and armor was being stripped from them; Jian supported and exhorted them, rousing them with loyalty and righteousness, and all shouted and fought with their utmost strength.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were frozen and starving, and some were stripping off their armor. Jian went among them, urging loyalty and righteousness, and they roared back into the fight.

sentences.zh: 瑊中流矢，進戰不輟，初不言痛。

translations.literal: Jian was struck by a flying arrow but pressed the attack without pause, never at first speaking of the pain.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was struck by an arrow but never slackened his attack and never mentioned the wound.

sentences.zh: 會雲梯輾地道，一輪偏陷，不能前卻，火從地中出，風勢亦回，城上人投葦炬，散松脂，沃以膏油，歡呼震地。

translations.literal: Just then the siege tower rolled over the tunnel; one wheel sank on one side and it could neither advance nor retreat; fire burst from the ground, the wind also shifted back, and men atop the wall threw reed torches, scattered pine resin, poured on grease and oil, their shouts shaking the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Just then a tower rolled over the tunnel. One wheel sank and the tower could neither advance nor retreat. Fire burst from below, the wind shifted, and defenders on the wall hurled reed torches, scattered pine resin, and poured on grease and oil. Their cheers shook the ground.

sentences.zh: 須臾，雲梯及梯上人皆為灰燼，臭聞數里，賊乃引退。

translations.literal: In an instant the siege towers and the men upon them were all reduced to ash; the stench was smelled for several li; the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In moments the towers and every man on them were reduced to ash. The stench carried for miles, and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於是三門皆出兵，太子親督戰，賊徒大敗，死者數千人。

translations.literal: Thereupon all three gates sent out troops; the crown prince personally directed the battle; the rebel host was utterly defeated, with several thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: All three gates sallied forth. The crown prince personally directed the battle. The rebels were routed, with thousands dead.

sentences.zh: 將士傷者，太子親為裹瘡。

translations.literal: For wounded officers and soldiers, the crown prince personally bound their wounds.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince personally dressed the wounds of the injured.

sentences.zh: 入夜，泚復來攻城，矢及御前三步而墜，上大驚。

translations.literal: At night Ci came again to attack the city; arrows reached within three paces of the emperor before falling; the emperor was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhu Ci attacked again. Arrows fell within three paces of the emperor before dropping to the ground. The emperor was terrified.

sentences.zh: 李懷光自蒲城引兵趣涇陽，並北山而西，先遣兵馬使張韶微服間行詣行在，藏表於蠟丸。

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang led troops from Pucheng toward Jingyang, following the northern mountains westward; he first sent the horse-and-army commissioner Zhang Shao in plain dress by secret route to the imperial presence, hiding his memorial in a wax pellet.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang marched from Pucheng toward Jingyang along the northern foothills. He first sent his cavalry commissioner Zhang Shao in disguise by a secret route to the emperor, with his memorial hidden in a wax pellet.

sentences.zh: 韶至奉天，值賊方攻城，見韶，以為賤人，驅之使與民俱填塹。

translations.literal: Shao reached Fengtian just as the rebels were attacking the city; seeing Shao, they took him for a lowly person and drove him to fill the moat together with the civilians.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao reached Fengtian the rebels were assaulting the walls. They took him for a common laborer and drove him to fill the moat with the civilians.

sentences.zh: 韶得間，逾塹抵城下呼曰：「我朔方軍使者也。」

translations.literal: Shao found an opening, crossed the moat, reached below the wall, and shouted: "I am an envoy of the Shuofang army!"
translations.idiomatic: Shao seized his chance, scrambled over the moat, and shouted up at the wall, "I am an envoy from the Shuofang army!"

sentences.zh: 城上人下繩引之，比登，身中數十矢，得表於衣中而進之。

translations.literal: Men atop the wall lowered a rope and drew him up; by the time he climbed up, he had been struck by several tens of arrows; he took the memorial from within his clothing and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Men on the wall lowered a rope and hauled him up. By the time he reached the top he had been struck by dozens of arrows. He drew the memorial from his clothing and presented it.

sentences.zh: 上大喜，舁韶以徇城，四隅歡聲如雷。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased; he had Shao carried around the city as a proclamation; from all four corners cheers thundered like rolling waves.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was overjoyed. He had Shao carried around the walls to announce the news, and cheers erupted from every corner like thunder.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，懷光敗泚兵於澧泉。

translations.literal: On guisi, Huaiguang defeated Ci's troops at Liquan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guisi, Li Huaiguang defeated Zhu Ci's army at Liquan.

sentences.zh: 泚聞之懼，引兵遁歸長安。

translations.literal: Ci, hearing this, was afraid and led his troops in flight back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci heard the news he was terrified and withdrew his army to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 眾以為懷光復三日不至，則城不守矣。

translations.literal: The multitude thought that if Huaiguang had been three days later in coming, the city could not have been held.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone agreed that if Li Huaiguang had been three days later, the city would not have held.

sentences.zh: 泚既退，從臣皆賀。

translations.literal: Once Ci had withdrawn, the attending ministers all offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci withdrew, the ministers who accompanied the emperor all offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 汴滑行營兵馬使賈隱林進言曰：「陛下性太急，不能容物，若此性未改，雖朱泚敗亡，憂未艾也！」

translations.literal: Jia Yinlin, horse-and-army commissioner of the Biansi campaign army, advanced and said: "Your Majesty's nature is too impatient and cannot tolerate others; if this nature is not changed, even though Zhu Ci is defeated and destroyed, your troubles will not cease!"
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yinlin, cavalry commissioner of the Bian campaign army, stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty is too quick-tempered and too little inclined to bear with others. Unless that changes, even when Zhu Ci is destroyed your troubles will not end!"

sentences.zh: 上不以為忤，甚稱之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not take it as an offense and greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took no offense and praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 侍御史-{万俟}-著開金、商運路，重圍既解，諸道貢賦繼至，用度始振。

translations.literal: The attendant censor Moqi Zhu opened the Jin and Shang transport routes; once the heavy siege was lifted, tribute and levies from the circuits arrived in succession, and expenditures began to recover.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant censor Moqi Zhu reopened the transport routes through Jin and Shang. Once the siege was lifted, tribute and supplies from the provinces began to arrive, and the court's finances began to recover.

sentences.zh: 朱泚至長安，但為城守之計，時遣人自城外來，周走呼曰：「奉天破矣！」

translations.literal: Zhu Ci, having reached Chang'an, made only plans for defending the city; from time to time he sent men from outside the city to run about calling: "Fengtian has fallen!
translations.idiomatic: Back in Chang'an, Zhu Ci devoted himself only to holding the city. From time to time he sent men out to run through the streets shouting, "Fengtian has fallen!

sentences.zh: 欲以惑眾。

translations.literal: wishing thereby to confuse the populace.
translations.idiomatic: Hoping to confuse the populace.

sentences.zh: 泚既據府庫之富，不愛金帛以悅將士，公卿家屬在城者皆給月俸。

translations.literal: Ci, having seized the wealth of the treasury stores, was not sparing of gold and silk in pleasing the officers and soldiers; the families of high ministers within the city were all given monthly stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Having seized the imperial treasuries, Zhu Ci lavished gold and silk on his officers and soldiers. He even paid monthly stipends to the families of high officials still trapped in the city.

sentences.zh: 神策及六軍從車駕及哥舒曜、李晟者，泚皆給其家糧。

translations.literal: For those of the Shence Army and the Six Armies who followed the imperial carriage, as well as Geshu Yao and Li Sheng, Zhu Ci all provided grain to their families.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci supplied grain to the families of every man in the Shence Army and the Six Armies who had followed the emperor's flight, as well as to the households of Geshu Yao and Li Sheng.

sentences.zh: 加以繕完器械，日費甚廣。

translations.literal: Added to this was the repair and completion of weapons and equipment; daily expenses were extremely vast.
translations.idiomatic: On top of that came the cost of repairing and replacing weapons and equipment, and daily expenditures grew enormous.

sentences.zh: 及長安平，府庫尚有餘蓄，見者皆追怨有司之暴斂焉。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was pacified, the treasury still held surplus stores, and those who saw it all lamented retrospectively the violent exactions of the officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang'an was recovered, the treasury still held large surpluses, and everyone who saw them looked back with bitter resentment at the officials' ruthless levies.

sentences.zh: 或謂泚曰：「陛下既受命，唐之陵庫不宜復存。」

translations.literal: Someone said to Zhu Ci: "Your Majesty has already received the Mandate; the mausoleums and treasuries of Tang ought not to be preserved any longer."
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Zhu Ci: "Your Majesty has already taken the throne — the Tang imperial tombs and treasuries should not be allowed to remain."

sentences.zh: 泚曰：「朕嘗北面事唐，豈忍為此！」

translations.literal: Zhu Ci said: "I once served Tang facing north as a subject — how could I bear to do such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci replied: "I once served the Tang court as a subject facing north — how could I bring myself to do that!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「百官多缺，請以兵脅士人補之。」

translations.literal: Again someone said: "Many offices among the hundred officials are vacant; I request that soldiers be used to coerce literati to fill them."
translations.idiomatic: Another proposal followed: "Many official posts stand empty — send soldiers to coerce scholars into accepting appointments."

sentences.zh: 泚曰：「強授之則人懼。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci said: "If offices are forcibly bestowed, people will be afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci said: "Force appointments on people and they will only be frightened.

sentences.zh: 但欲仕者則與之，何必叩戶拜官邪！」

translations.literal: Give appointments only to those who wish to take office — why must we go knocking door to door to hand out posts!"
translations.idiomatic: Give office only to those who want to serve — why go door to door pressing commissions on people!"

sentences.zh: 所用者惟范陽、神策團練兵。

translations.literal: Those he employed were only the regimental-trained troops of Fanyang and the Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: The only men he actually relied on were the regimental troops of Fanyang and the Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 涇原卒驕，皆不為用，但守其所掠資貨，不肯出戰。

translations.literal: The Jingyuan troops were arrogant and would none of them serve; they merely guarded the goods they had plundered and refused to go out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingyuan soldiers, insubordinate and arrogant, would not fight for him at all; they merely hoarded their plunder and refused to take the field.

sentences.zh: 又密謀殺泚，不果而止。

translations.literal: They also secretly plotted to kill Zhu Ci, but when it did not succeed they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They also plotted secretly to assassinate Zhu Ci; when the attempt failed, they abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 李懷光性粗疏，自山東來赴難，數與人言盧杞、趙贊、白志貞之奸佞，且曰：「天下之亂，皆此曹所為也！

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang was coarse and careless by nature. Coming from Shandong to rescue the court in crisis, he repeatedly told others of the treachery and flattery of Lu Qi, Zhao Zan, and Bai Zhizhen, and said: "The turmoil throughout the realm is all the doing of these men!
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang was blunt and rough by temperament. Marching from Shandong to relieve the throne in its distress, he often denounced Lu Qi, Zhao Zan, and Bai Zhizhen as treacherous flatterers, declaring: "The chaos engulfing the empire is entirely their work!

sentences.zh: 吾見上，當請誅之。」

translations.literal: When I see the Emperor, I shall request that they be executed."
translations.idiomatic: When I see the emperor, I shall ask that they be put to death."

sentences.zh: 既解奉天之圍，自矜其功，謂上必接以殊禮。

translations.literal: After he had lifted the siege of Fengtian, he took pride in his achievement and believed the Emperor would surely receive him with extraordinary honors.
translations.idiomatic: After breaking the siege of Fengtian, he grew proud of his achievement and expected the emperor to greet him with exceptional honors.

sentences.zh: 或說王翃、趙贊曰：「懷光緣道憤歎，以為宰相謀議乖方，度支賦斂煩重，京尹犒賜刻薄。

translations.literal: Someone told Wang Hong and Zhao Zan: "Huaiguang, all along the road, has been indignant and sighing, claiming that the chancellor's policies are misguided, that the Department of Public Revenue's levies are oppressively heavy, and that the capital intendant's rewards and gifts are stingy.
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned Wang Hong and Zhao Zan: "All along the march Huaiguang has been venting his anger, blaming the chancellor for misguided counsel, the revenue commissioner for crushing taxes, and the capital prefect for miserly rewards.

sentences.zh: 致乘輿播遷者，三臣之罪也。

translations.literal: The fault of these three ministers is what caused the imperial carriage to be driven from place to place.
translations.idiomatic: It was these three ministers, he says, who drove the emperor from his capital.

sentences.zh: 今懷光新立大功，上必披襟布誠，詢訪得失，使其言入，豈不殆哉！」

translations.literal: Now Huaiguang has just established a great merit; the Emperor is sure to open his heart in sincerity and inquire about what has gone right and wrong. If Huaiguang's words are allowed in, will we not be in peril!"
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang has just won a great victory — the emperor is certain to open his heart and ask what has gone wrong. If Huaiguang's accusations reach the throne, will we not be ruined!"

sentences.zh: 翃、贊以告盧杞。

translations.literal: Wang Hong and Zhao Zan reported this to Lu Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong and Zhao Zan relayed this to Lu Qi.

sentences.zh: 杞懼，從容言於上曰：「懷光勳業，社稷是賴，賊徒破膽，皆無守心，若使之乘勝取長安，則一舉可以滅賊，此破竹之勢也，今聽其入朝，必當賜宴，留連累日，使賊入京城，得從容成備，恐難圖矣！」

translations.literal: Lu Qi was alarmed and, speaking calmly to the Emperor, said: "Huaiguang's achievements are what the altars of soil and grain rely upon; the rebel bandits have lost their nerve and all lack the will to hold their ground. If he is allowed to press his victory and take Chang'an, the rebels can be destroyed in a single stroke — this is a momentum that splits bamboo. But if he is now permitted to enter court for an audience, he will certainly be granted a banquet and detained for days on end, giving the rebels time to enter the capital and prepare their defenses at leisure — I fear they will then be hard to overcome!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi was frightened and, speaking calmly to the emperor, said: "Huaiguang's merit is the state's mainstay; the rebels are already terrified and have lost the will to hold out. Let him press his advantage and take Chang'an, and the rebels can be wiped out at one stroke — the momentum will be like splitting bamboo. But if he is summoned to court now, he will surely be feasted and kept for days, giving the rebels time to re-enter the capital and fortify it at leisure — then they may prove impossible to defeat!"

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The Emperor thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔懷光直引軍屯便橋，與李建徽、李晟及神策兵馬使楊惠元刻期共取長安。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Huaiguang to lead his army straightaway to encamp at Bian Bridge, and at a fixed date to take Chang'an jointly with Li Jianhui, Li Sheng, and the Shence Army cavalry commissioner Yang Huiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed Huaiguang to march straight to Bian Bridge with his army and, on a fixed date, join Li Jianhui, Li Sheng, and Shence cavalry commissioner Yang Huiyuan in a joint assault on Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 懷光自以數千里竭誠赴難，破朱泚，解重圍，而咫尺不得見天子，意殊怏怏，曰：「吾今已為奸臣所排，事可知矣！」

translations.literal: Huaiguang considered that he had traveled thousands of li in utmost loyalty to answer the crisis, had defeated Zhu Ci, and lifted a grave siege, yet at arm's length could not see the Son of Heaven. He was deeply resentful and said: "I have now been pushed aside by treacherous ministers — how affairs will go is already plain!"
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang felt he had marched thousands of li in loyal haste to save the throne, had broken Zhu Ci and lifted a desperate siege, yet could not even get an audience with the emperor though he stood so near. Deeply aggrieved, he said: "Treacherous ministers have already shut me out — I can see how this will end!"

sentences.zh: 遂引兵去，至魯店，留二日乃行。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led his army away; when he reached Ludian he halted two days before moving on.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched away; at Ludian he halted two days before continuing.

sentences.zh: 劍南西山兵馬使張朏以所部兵作亂，入成都，西川節度使張延賞棄城奔漢州。

translations.literal: Zhang Fei, military commissioner of the Western Mountains in Jiannan, raised a mutiny with the troops under his command, entered Chengdu, and Zhang Yanshang, military governor of Xichuan, abandoned the city and fled to Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fei, military commissioner of the Western Mountains in Jiannan, mutinied with his command, entered Chengdu, and Zhang Yanshang, governor of Xichuan, abandoned the city and fled to Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 鹿頭戍將叱干遂等討之，斬朏及其黨，延賞復歸成都。

translations.literal: Chi Gansui and others, garrison commanders at Lutou Fort, marched against them, beheaded Zhang Fei and his faction, and Yanshang returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Gansui and other commanders at Lutou Fort marched against them, executed Zhang Fei and his followers, and Yanshang returned to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使陳少游將兵討李希烈，屯盱眙，聞朱泚作亂，歸廣陵，修塹壘，繕甲兵。

translations.literal: Chen Shaoyou, military governor of Huainan, had been leading troops against Li Xilie and was encamped at Xuyi. On hearing that Zhu Ci had rebelled, he returned to Guangling, repaired ditches and ramparts, and maintained armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou, military governor of Huainan, had been campaigning against Li Xilie from a base at Xuyi. When he heard of Zhu Ci's rebellion, he withdrew to Guangling, dug trenches, built ramparts, and readied arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 浙江東、西節度使韓滉閉關梁，禁馬牛出境，築石頭城，穿井近百所，繕館第數十，修塢壁，起建業，抵京峴，樓堞相屬，以備車駕渡江，且自固也。

translations.literal: Han Huang, military governor of Zhedong and Xixi in Zhejiang, closed the passes at Liang, forbade horses and cattle to leave the border, built Shitou Fortress, dug nearly a hundred wells, constructed dozens of mansions and lodges, repaired embankments and walls, and erected fortifications from Jianye to Jingxian with watchtowers and parapets linking one to the next, both to prepare for the imperial carriage's crossing the Yangzi and to fortify himself.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang, governor of Zhedong and Xixi in Zhejiang, sealed the passes at Liang, barred horses and cattle from leaving the region, built Shitou Fortress, sank nearly a hundred wells, erected dozens of mansions, repaired embankments and walls, and raised fortifications from Jianye to Jingxian with linked towers and battlements — both to prepare for the emperor's possible crossing of the Yangzi and to strengthen his own position.

sentences.zh: 少游發兵三千大閱於江北。

translations.literal: Shaoyou dispatched three thousand troops for a grand review north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou mustered three thousand men for a grand review north of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 滉亦發舟師三千曜武於京江以應之。

translations.literal: Huang likewise dispatched three thousand naval troops to display their might on the Jingjiang in response.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang answered with three thousand warships, parading his strength on the Jing River.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵使包佶有錢帛八百萬、將輸京師。

translations.literal: Bao Ji, commissioner of salt and iron, had eight million strings of cash and silk goods and was about to transport them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Ji, commissioner of salt and iron, held eight million strings' worth of cash and silk and was preparing to ship them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 陳少游以為賊據長安，未期收復，欲強取之。

translations.literal: Chen Shaoyou reasoned that with the rebels holding Chang'an, recovery could not be expected soon, and wished to seize the goods by force.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou reasoned that with rebels holding Chang'an, the capital would not be recovered anytime soon, and tried to seize the funds by force.

sentences.zh: 佶不可，少游欲殺之。

translations.literal: Bao Ji refused; Shaoyou wanted to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Ji refused; Shaoyou then wanted him killed.

sentences.zh: 佶懼，匿妻子於案牘中，急濟江。

translations.literal: Bao Ji was terrified; he hid his wife and children among the document boxes and hurriedly crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Bao Ji hid his wife and children among the document chests and fled hastily across the river.

sentences.zh: 少游悉收其錢帛。

translations.literal: Shaoyou confiscated all his cash and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou seized all the cash and silk.

sentences.zh: 佶有守財卒三千，少游亦奪之。

translations.literal: Bao Ji had three thousand troops guarding the treasure; Shaoyou seized them as well.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Ji also had three thousand troops guarding the treasury; Shaoyou took them too.

sentences.zh: 佶才與數十人俱至上元，復為韓滉所奪。

translations.literal: Bao Ji had barely reached Shangyuan with several dozen men when he was plundered again by Han Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Ji had barely reached Shangyuan with a few dozen followers when Han Huang stripped him again.

sentences.zh: 時南方籓鎮各閉境自守，惟曹王皋數遣使開道貢獻。

translations.literal: At this time the southern frontier commands each closed their borders and held themselves aloof; only Prince Cao Li Gao repeatedly sent envoys to open routes and present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the southern regional commands mostly sealed their borders and looked to their own defense; only Prince of Cao Li Gao repeatedly sent envoys to clear routes and deliver tribute.

sentences.zh: 李希烈攻逼汴、鄭，江、淮路絕，朝貢皆自宣、饒、荊、襄趣武關。

translations.literal: Li Xilie pressed his attack on Bian and Zheng; routes through the Yangzi and Huai were cut off, and tribute missions all traveled from Xuan, Rao, Jing, and Xiang toward Wuguan.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Xilie pressing Bian and Zheng, routes through the Jiang and Huai regions were severed, and tribute missions had to travel from Xuancheng, Raozhou, Jingzhou, and Xiangyang toward Wuguan.

sentences.zh: 皋治郵驛，平道路，由是往來之使，通行無阻。

translations.literal: Gao maintained postal stations and cleared the roads; henceforth envoys traveling back and forth passed without obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Gao restored the postal stations and repaired the roads, so envoys traveling to and fro could pass without hindrance.

sentences.zh: 上問陸贄以當今切務。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Lu Zhi about the most urgent tasks of the present day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Lu Zhi what the most pressing business of the day was.

sentences.zh: 贄以曏日致亂，由上下之情不通，勸上接下從諫，乃上疏，其略曰：「臣謂當今急務，在於審察群情，若群情之所甚欲者，陛下先行之；

translations.literal: Lu Zhi held that the disorder of recent days arose from failure of communication between above and below, and urged the Emperor to be approachable and accept remonstrance. He then submitted a memorial, the gist of which ran: "Your servant holds that the urgent task of the present lies in carefully examining the feelings of the multitude. Whatever the multitude deeply desires, Your Majesty should undertake first;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi argued that the recent turmoil stemmed from a breakdown between ruler and ruled, and urged the emperor to be approachable and heed remonstrance. He submitted a memorial whose gist was: "Your servant believes the urgent task today is to read the mood of the people. Whatever the people most desire, Your Majesty should do first;

sentences.zh: 所甚惡者，陛下先去之。

translations.literal: whatever they deeply abhor, Your Majesty should remove first.
translations.idiomatic: whatever they most hate, Your Majesty should abolish first.

sentences.zh: 欲惡與天下同而天下不歸者，自古及今，未之有也。

translations.literal: One who shares desires and aversions with all under Heaven yet fails to win the allegiance of all under Heaven — from antiquity to the present, there has never been such a case.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity to the present, no ruler who shared the people's loves and hates has ever failed to win their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 未理亂之本，繫於人心，況乎當變故動搖之時，在危疑向背之際，人之所歸則植，人之所在則傾，陛下安可不審察群情，同其欲惡，使億兆歸趣，以靖邦家乎！

translations.literal: The root of order and disorder lies in the hearts of the people — how much more so in a time of upheaval and instability, at a moment of crisis and wavering loyalty, when where the people turn thrives and where they turn away topples! How can Your Majesty fail to examine the feelings of the multitude, share their desires and aversions, and bring the hundred millions to rally, so as to settle the realm and household!
translations.idiomatic: The root of order and chaos lies in the hearts of the people — all the more so in times of upheaval, when loyalty wavers and where the people turn flourishes while where they turn away collapses. How can Your Majesty fail to read the public mood, align with their loves and hates, and draw the masses back to restore peace to the realm!

sentences.zh: 此誠當今之所急也。」

translations.literal: This is truly what is urgent today."
translations.idiomatic: This is truly the most urgent matter of the day."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「頃者竊聞輿議，頗究群情，四方則患於中外意乖，百辟又患於君臣道隔。

translations.literal: Again he wrote: "Recently I have privately heard public discussion, which has examined the feelings of the multitude with some care: in the four directions the worry is that court and regions are at odds in mind; among the hundred officials the worry is that the way between monarch and minister is blocked.
translations.idiomatic: He continued: "I have lately overheard public talk probing the mood of the realm: in the provinces the fear is that court and regions are at cross purposes; among officials the fear is that the bond between ruler and minister has been severed.

sentences.zh: 郡國之志不達於朝廷，朝廷之誠不升於軒陛。

translations.literal: The intent of the commanderies and states does not reach the court; the sincerity of the court does not ascend to the imperial steps.
translations.idiomatic: The wishes of the provinces never reach the court, and the court's sincerity never ascends to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上澤闕於下布，下情壅於上聞，實事不必知，知事不必實，上下否隔於其際，真偽雜糅於其間，聚怨囂囂，騰謗籍籍，欲無疑阻，其可得乎！」

translations.literal: Imperial grace fails to spread below; sentiments below choke off from reaching above. True circumstances need not be known; what is known need not be true. Above and below are severed at their juncture; truth and falsehood are mingled in between. Resentments gather clamorously; slander rises in swarms — to expect no doubt and obstruction, how is that possible!"
translations.idiomatic: Imperial favor does not reach the people below; their grievances do not reach the throne above. Facts need not be known, and what is known need not be true. Above and below are cut off from each other; truth and falsehood are tangled together. Resentment gathers and slander spreads — how can there be no distrust and obstruction!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「總天下之智以助聰明，順天下之心以施教令，則君臣同志，何有不從！

translations.literal: Again: "Gather the wisdom of all under Heaven to assist Your Majesty's intelligence; follow the hearts of all under Heaven in issuing edicts and commands — then monarch and ministers will share one purpose; what would not be obeyed!
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Pool the wisdom of the empire to sharpen Your Majesty's judgment; align edicts with the people's hearts — then ruler and ministers will act as one, and who would not obey!

sentences.zh: 遠邇歸心，孰與為亂！」

translations.literal: Near and far will turn their hearts in allegiance — who will join in rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: Near and far will give their hearts to the throne — who would then dare rebel!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「慮有愚而近道，事有要而似迂。」

translations.literal: Again: "There is counsel that seems foolish yet nears the Way; there are matters of vital importance that seem roundabout."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Some advice seems foolish yet is close to the Way; some essential matters look impractical yet are vital."

sentences.zh: 疏奏旬日，上無所施行，亦不詰問。

translations.literal: Ten days after the memorial was submitted, the Emperor neither implemented anything nor questioned him about it.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days passed after the memorial was submitted; the emperor neither acted on it nor asked Lu Zhi about it.

sentences.zh: 贄又上疏，其略曰：「臣聞立國之本，在乎得眾，得眾之要，在乎見情。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi submitted another memorial, the gist of which ran: "Your servant has heard that the foundation of establishing a state lies in winning the multitude; the key to winning the multitude lies in seeing their true sentiments.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi submitted another memorial, writing in essence: "Your servant has heard that the foundation of a state is winning the people, and the key to winning the people is understanding their true feelings.

sentences.zh: 故仲尼以謂人情者聖王之田，言理道所生也。」

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius called the human sentiments the field of the sage-king, meaning that right governance grows from them."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius therefore called human sentiment the sage-king's field — the soil from which right governance grows."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「《易》，乾下坤上曰泰，坤下乾上曰否，損上益下曰益，損下益上曰損。

translations.literal: Again: "In the Book of Changes, with Qian below and Kun above it is called Tai; with Kun below and Qian above it is called Pi; diminishing the above and enriching the below is called Yi (Increase); diminishing the below and enriching the above is called Sun (Decrease).
translations.idiomatic: He continued: "In the Book of Changes, Qian below and Kun above forms Tai; Kun below and Qian above forms Pi. Diminishing the upper and enriching the lower is called Increase; diminishing the lower and enriching the upper is called Decrease.

sentences.zh: 夫天在下而地處上，於位乖矣，而反謂之泰者，上下交故也。

translations.literal: Heaven is below and earth is above — in position this is awry — yet it is called Tai because above and below intercommunicate.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven below and earth above is a reversal of their proper places, yet the hexagram is called Peace — because upper and lower communicate.

sentences.zh: 君在上而臣處下，於義順矣，而反謂之否者，上下不交故也。

translations.literal: The ruler is above and ministers below — in principle this is proper — yet it is called Pi because above and below do not intercommunicate.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler above and ministers below accords with propriety, yet the hexagram is called Obstruction — because upper and lower do not communicate.

sentences.zh: 上約己而裕於人，人必悅而奉上矣，豈不謂之益乎！

translations.literal: If the ruler restrains himself and is generous toward others, others will surely rejoice and serve the ruler — is this not what we call Increase!
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler restrains himself and is generous to others, the people will gladly serve him — is that not Increase!

sentences.zh: 上蔑人而肆諸己，人必怨而叛上矣，豈不謂之損乎！」

translations.literal: If the ruler scorns others and indulges himself, others will surely resent and rebel against the ruler — is this not what we call Decrease!"
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler despises others and indulges himself, the people will resent and turn against him — is that not Decrease!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「舟即君道，水即人情。

translations.literal: Again: "The boat is the way of the ruler; the water is the disposition of the people.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote further: "The boat is the way of the ruler; the water is the temper of the people.

sentences.zh: 舟順水之道乃浮，違則沒；

translations.literal: A boat that follows the course of the water floats; violate it and it sinks;
translations.idiomatic: A boat that follows the water stays afloat; fight the current and it sinks;

sentences.zh: 君得人之情乃固，失則危。

translations.literal: a ruler who gains the people's disposition is secure; lose it and he is endangered.
translations.idiomatic: a ruler who holds the people's hearts is secure; lose them and he is in peril.

sentences.zh: 是以古先聖王之居人上也，必以其欲從天下之心，而不敢以天下之人從其欲。」

translations.literal: Therefore the sage-kings of old, dwelling above others, surely aligned their desires with the hearts of all under Heaven, and dared not make all under Heaven align with their desires."
translations.idiomatic: That is why the sage-kings of old, though they ruled above others, always shaped their own wishes to the hearts of the people, and never forced the people to follow their personal desires."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「陛下憤習俗以妨理，任削平而在躬，以明威照臨，以嚴法制斷，流弊自久，浚恆太深。

translations.literal: Again: "Your Majesty, indignant that custom obstructs good governance, has taken suppression and pacification upon himself, governing with manifest authority and stern law to judge cases — yet the corrupt practices are long-standing and the dredging goes too deep.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Your Majesty, angry that entrenched custom obstructs good government, has taken harsh suppression upon yourself, ruling with open severity and stern law — yet these abuses are of long standing, and the cure has cut too deep.

sentences.zh: 遠者驚疑而阻命逃死之亂作，近者畏懾而偷容避罪之態生。

translations.literal: Those far away are startled and doubtful, and disorder of defying orders and fleeing for one's life arises; those nearby are awed and afraid, and an attitude of going through the motions to avoid punishment emerges.
translations.idiomatic: Those far off grow alarmed and defy orders or flee for their lives; those nearby cower and merely go through the motions to avoid punishment.

sentences.zh: 君臣意乖，上下情隔，君務致理，而下防誅夷，臣將納忠，又上慮欺誕，故睿誠不佈於群物，物情不達於睿聰。

translations.literal: Monarch and ministers are at odds in mind; above and below are estranged in sentiment. The ruler strives for order, yet below guards against execution and extinction; ministers would offer loyalty, yet above worries about deceit and falsehood. Thus sagely sincerity does not reach the myriad things, and the disposition of things does not reach sagely understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and ministers are estranged; above and below no longer understand each other. The emperor seeks good order, yet officials below fear execution; ministers wish to offer loyal counsel, yet the throne suspects deception. Sagely sincerity never reaches the world, and the world's feelings never reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 臣於往年曾任御史，獲奉朝謁，僅欲半年，陛下嚴邃高居，未嘗降旨臨問，群臣跼蹐趨退，亦不列事奏陳。

translations.literal: Your servant, in former years, once served as censor and obtained audience at court — barely half a year in all. Your Majesty sat high in stern seclusion and never issued a directive to question in person; the assembled ministers, cramped and constrained, hurried forward and retreated, and also did not lay out matters for memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant once served as censor and attended court audiences for barely half a year. Your Majesty remained aloof and stern, never descending to question officials in person. Ministers approached and withdrew in cramped silence and did not lay matters before the throne.

sentences.zh: 軒墀之間，且未相諭，宇宙之廣，何由自通！

translations.literal: Between the hall and the steps, understanding had not even been exchanged — in the vastness of the cosmos, how could communication arise of itself!
translations.idiomatic: Within the hall itself there was no real exchange — in a realm so vast, how could truth ever reach the throne on its own!

sentences.zh: 雖復例對使臣，別延宰輔，既殊師錫，且異公言。

translations.literal: Even though audiences with envoys followed precedent and the chief ministers were separately summoned, this differed from the instruction of the masters and also from open counsel among peers.
translations.idiomatic: Even when envoys were received by routine and chief ministers were summoned separately, this was not the same as instruction from one's teachers, nor the same as open counsel among colleagues.

sentences.zh: 未行者則戒以樞密勿論，已行者又謂之遂事不諫，漸生拘礙，動涉猜嫌，由是人各隱情，以言為諱，至於變亂將起，億兆同憂，獨陛下恬然不知，方謂太平可致。

translations.literal: Those not yet in office were warned that state secrets must not be discussed; those who had already acted were told that completed matters must not be remonstrated against. Gradually constraints arose; every move touched suspicion — hence each person hid his true feelings and treated speech as taboo. When rebellion was about to break out, the hundred millions shared the same anxiety, yet Your Majesty alone remained placid and unaware, still believing that great peace could be attained.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had not yet acted were warned not to discuss state secrets; those who had already acted were told that what was done could not be remonstrated against. Constraints multiplied; every word bred suspicion. Each man hid his true feelings and feared to speak. When rebellion was about to erupt and the whole people shared one dread, Your Majesty alone remained untroubled, still believing peace was at hand.

sentences.zh: 陛下以今日之所睹驗往時之所聞，孰真孰虛，何得何失，則事之通塞備詳之矣！

translations.literal: Let Your Majesty verify by what you witness today what you heard in times past — which was true and which false, what succeeded and what failed — then the full course of affairs, blocked or open, will be thoroughly known!
translations.idiomatic: Let Your Majesty test what you once heard against what you see today — what was true and what false, what succeeded and what failed — and the full truth of how affairs stand will become clear!

sentences.zh: 人之情偽盡知之矣！」

translations.literal: The truth and falsehood of human sentiment will be wholly understood!"
translations.idiomatic: The truth and falsehood of men's hearts will be fully known!"

sentences.zh: 上乃遣中使諭之曰：「朕本性甚好推誠，亦能納諫。

translations.literal: The Emperor then sent a palace emissary to instruct him, saying: "By nature I greatly favor extending sincerity and can also accept remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent a palace envoy to reply: "By nature I greatly favor openness and sincerity, and I am willing to accept remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 將謂君臣一體，全不堤防，緣推誠信不疑，多被奸人賣弄。

translations.literal: I thought that ruler and ministers were one body and did not guard against anything at all. Because I extended sincerity and trusted without doubt, I was often played and manipulated by treacherous men.
translations.idiomatic: I thought ruler and ministers were one body and needed no guard at all. Because I trusted openly and without suspicion, treacherous men often played upon me.

sentences.zh: 今所致患害，朕思亦無它，其失反在推誠。

translations.literal: The harm that has now been brought about — I consider there is no other cause; the failure lies rather in extending sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: The harm that has come of this, I believe, has no other root: the failure lies in being too trusting.

sentences.zh: 又，諫官論事，少能慎密，例自矜衒，歸過於朕以自取名。

translations.literal: Furthermore, when remonstrating officials discuss affairs, few can be discreet; as a rule they boast and show off, attributing blame to me in order to make a name for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, remonstrating officials rarely keep matters discreet; as a rule they boast and parade themselves, blaming me to win a reputation.

sentences.zh: 朕從即位以來，見奏對論事者甚多，大抵皆是雷同，道聽塗說，試加質問，遽即辭窮。

translations.literal: Since my accession I have seen very many who memorialized or answered in audience on affairs; for the most part their views were identical, hearsay picked up along the way — when questioned, they immediately had no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Since my accession I have heard many officials memorializing or answering at audience on affairs; for the most part their views were identical, picked up from hearsay — question them and they immediately have nothing to say.

sentences.zh: 若有奇才異能，在朕豈惜拔擢？

translations.literal: If there were men of extraordinary talent and ability, would I begrudge promoting them?
translations.idiomatic: If there were men of real talent and ability, would I begrudge promoting them?

sentences.zh: 朕見從前已來，事只如此，所以近來不多取次對人，亦非倦於接納。

translations.literal: I see that from the past until now affairs have been only like this; therefore of late I have not often granted audiences casually — this is not because I am weary of receiving people.
translations.idiomatic: I see that things have always been this way, which is why of late I have not often granted casual audiences — not because I am weary of receiving people.

sentences.zh: 卿宜深悉此意。」

translations.literal: You, sir, should fully understand this intent."
translations.idiomatic: You should understand this fully."

sentences.zh: 贄以人君臨下，當以誠信為本。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi held that a ruler governing those below ought to take sincerity and trust as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi held that a ruler governing his subjects must take sincerity and trust as his foundation.

sentences.zh: 諫者雖辭情鄙拙，亦當優容以開言路，若震之以威，折之以辯，則臣下何敢盡言，乃復上疏，其略曰：「天子之道，與天同方，天不以地有惡木而廢發生，天子不以時有小人而廢聽納。」

translations.literal: Even if remonstrators' words were crude and clumsy, they ought still to be treated with forbearance to open the path of speech. If they were awed by authority or refuted by disputation, how would officials below dare speak fully? He then submitted yet another memorial, the gist of which ran: "The way of the Son of Heaven shares Heaven's direction: Heaven does not cease nurturing life because the earth has vicious trees; the Son of Heaven does not cease listening and accepting because the time has petty men."
translations.idiomatic: Even when remonstrators' words were crude or awkward, they should still be treated with forbearance to keep the path of speech open. If they were cowed by authority or silenced by argument, how could officials below dare speak freely? He submitted yet another memorial, writing in essence: "The way of the Son of Heaven follows Heaven's example: Heaven does not cease to nurture life because the earth holds poisonous trees; the Son of Heaven should not cease to listen and accept counsel because the age has petty men."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「唯信與誠，有失無補。

translations.literal: Again: "In sincerity and trust alone, once lost there is no remedy.
translations.idiomatic: He continued: "In sincerity and trust alone, once lost there is no restoring them.

sentences.zh: 一不誠則心莫之保，一不信則言莫之行。

translations.literal: One moment without sincerity and the heart cannot be preserved; one moment without trust and words cannot be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: One lapse of sincerity and the heart cannot be kept; one lapse of trust and words cannot be obeyed.

sentences.zh: 陛下所謂失於誠信以致患害者，臣竊以斯言為過矣。」

translations.literal: What Your Majesty calls failing through sincerity and trust and thereby bringing harm — your servant privately considers those words excessive."
translations.idiomatic: What Your Majesty calls having failed through sincerity and trust and thereby brought harm — your servant privately believes that judgment goes too far."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「馭之以智則人詐，示之以疑則人偷。

translations.literal: Again: "Govern people with cunning and they will feign; show them suspicion and they will be furtive.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Rule people with cunning and they will dissemble; show them suspicion and they will become furtive.

sentences.zh: 上行之則下從之，上施之則下報之。

translations.literal: What the ruler practices, those below follow; what the ruler applies, those below return in kind.
translations.idiomatic: What the ruler practices, those below follow; what the ruler shows, those below return in kind.

sentences.zh: 若誠不盡於己而望盡於人，眾必怠而不從矣。

translations.literal: If sincerity is not complete in oneself yet one expects completeness in others, the multitude will surely slacken and not follow.
translations.idiomatic: If one is not fully sincere oneself yet expects full sincerity from others, the people will slacken and refuse to follow.

sentences.zh: 不誠於前而曰誠於後，眾心疑而不信矣。

translations.literal: If one was not sincere before yet speaks of sincerity afterward, hearts will doubt and not believe.
translations.idiomatic: If one was insincere before yet speaks of sincerity afterward, hearts will doubt and refuse to believe.

sentences.zh: 是知誠信之道，不可斯須而去身。

translations.literal: From this we know that the way of sincerity and trust cannot for an instant depart from one's person.
translations.idiomatic: From this we know that sincerity and trust cannot for a moment be set aside.

sentences.zh: 願陛下慎守而行之有加，恐非所以為悔者也！」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would carefully keep to it and practice it ever more — I fear that is not grounds for regret!"
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to guard it carefully and practice it ever more faithfully — that is no cause for regret!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「臣聞仲虺讚揚成湯，不稱其無過而稱其改過；

translations.literal: Again: "Your servant has heard that Zhong Hui praised King Cheng Tang — not calling him free of faults but praising his correcting faults;
translations.idiomatic: He wrote further: "Your servant has heard that Zhong Hui praised King Tang of Shang — not for having no faults, but for correcting his faults;

sentences.zh: 吉甫歌誦周宣，不美其無闕而美其補闕。

translations.literal: Jifu sang in praise of King Xuan of Zhou — not commending him for having no flaws but commending him for filling in what was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu sang the praises of King Xuan of Zhou — not for being flawless, but for mending what was lacking.

sentences.zh: 是則聖賢之意較然著明，惟以改過為能，不以無過為貴。

translations.literal: Thus the intent of sages and worthies is comparatively clear and plain: they value only the ability to reform faults, not the possession of no faults.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the intent of the sages is clear: they valued the ability to reform faults, not the possession of no faults.

sentences.zh: 蓋為人之行己，必有過差，上智下愚，俱所不免，智者改過而遷善，愚者恥過而遂非；

translations.literal: For in how people conduct themselves there must be errors and lapses — neither the highest wisdom nor the lowest foolishness can altogether avoid them. The wise reform faults and move toward goodness; the foolish are shamed by faults and persist in wrong;
translations.idiomatic: For in how people conduct themselves there are always errors and lapses — neither the wisest nor the most foolish can wholly avoid them. The wise reform their faults and turn toward goodness; the foolish are shamed by faults and persist in wrong;

sentences.zh: 遷善則其德日新，遂非則其惡彌積。」

translations.literal: Moving toward goodness, their virtue daily renews; persisting in wrong, their evil ever accumulates."
translations.idiomatic: Turn toward goodness and virtue renews day by day; persist in wrong and evil accumulates ever deeper."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「諫官不密自矜，信非忠厚，其於聖德固亦無虧。

translations.literal: Again: "That remonstrating officials are indiscreet and boast of themselves — truly this is not deep loyalty; yet it in no way diminishes Your Majesty's sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "That remonstrating officials are indiscreet and boastful is indeed not deep loyalty — yet it in no way diminishes Your Majesty's sagely virtue.

sentences.zh: 陛下若納諫不違，則傳之適足增美；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty accepts remonstrance without turning away, then for such talk to spread would only add to your luster;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty accepts remonstrance without turning away, then for such talk to spread would only add to your glory;

sentences.zh: 陛下若違諫不納，又安能禁之勿傳！」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty turns from remonstrance and will not accept it, how could you forbid it from spreading!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty turns from remonstrance and refuses to heed it, how can you forbid it from spreading!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「侈言無驗不必用，質言當理不必違。

translations.literal: Again: "Lofty words without verification need not be used; plain words that accord with principle need not be rejected.
translations.idiomatic: He continued: "Grand words that cannot be verified need not be acted on; plain words that fit reason need not be rejected.

sentences.zh: 辭拙而效速者不必愚，言甘而利重者不必智。

translations.literal: One whose words are clumsy yet whose effects come quickly need not be foolish; one whose words are sweet yet whose benefits are heavy need not be wise.
translations.idiomatic: A man whose speech is awkward but whose results come quickly is not necessarily a fool; a man whose words are honeyed but whose gains are great is not necessarily wise.

sentences.zh: 是皆考之以實，慮之以終，其用無它，唯善所在。」

translations.literal: All these should be tested by facts and considered to their end; there is no other use but where goodness lies."
translations.idiomatic: All of this should be tested against facts and weighed to the end — the only standard is where the good lies."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「陛下所謂『比見奏對論事皆是雷同道聽塗說者』。

translations.literal: Again: "What Your Majesty calls 'those who memorialized and answered on affairs of late being all identical, repeating hearsay picked up along the way.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "As for what Your Majesty said — that those who have lately memorialized and answered at audience on affairs all repeat the same thing, parroting street gossip —

sentences.zh: 臣竊以眾多之議，足見人情，必有可行，亦有可畏，恐不宜一概輕侮而莫之省納也。

translations.literal: Your servant privately holds that the abundance of such opinions fully reflects human sentiment — there must be what can be implemented and also what should be feared; I fear it is not right to dismiss them all lightly and refuse to examine and accept any.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant believes that so many voices together reveal the temper of the people — some of it must be worth acting on, and some of it worth fearing. I fear it is wrong to dismiss the whole lot with contempt and refuse to examine and accept any of it.

sentences.zh: 陛下又謂『試加質問，即便辭窮』者，臣但以陛下雖窮其辭而未窮其理，能服其口而未服其心。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty also said 'when questioned they immediately have no reply' — your servant holds only that though Your Majesty has exhausted their words, you have not exhausted their principles; you have silenced their mouths but not won their hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty also said that when questioned, they immediately have nothing to say. Your servant holds only that though Your Majesty may exhaust their words, you have not exhausted their reasoning; you may silence their mouths, but you have not won their hearts."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「為下者莫不願忠，為上者莫不求理。

translations.literal: Again: "Those below all wish to be loyal; those above all seek right governance.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote further: "Those below all wish to be loyal; those above all seek good order.

sentences.zh: 然而下每苦上之不理，上每苦下之不忠。

translations.literal: Yet those below always suffer that those above are unresponsive; those above always suffer that those below are disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those below always complain that those above will not heed them, and those above always complain that those below are not loyal.

sentences.zh: 若是者何？

translations.literal: If that is so, why?
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, why is it so?

sentences.zh: 兩情不通故也。

translations.literal: Because the sentiments of the two sides do not communicate.
translations.idiomatic: Because the feelings of the two sides do not reach each other.

sentences.zh: 下之情莫不願達於上，上之情莫不求知於下，然而下恆苦上之難達，上恆苦下之難知。

translations.literal: The sentiments of those below all wish to reach those above; the sentiments of those above all seek to be known by those below — yet those below always suffer that those above are hard to reach, and those above always suffer that those below are hard to know.
translations.idiomatic: Those below all wish their feelings to reach the throne; those above all wish to know the feelings of those below — yet those below always find those above hard to reach, and those above always find those below hard to know.

sentences.zh: 若是者何？

translations.literal: If that is so, why?
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, why is it so?

sentences.zh: 九弊不去故也。
