translations.literal: Because the nine abuses have not been removed.
translations.idiomatic: It is because the nine abuses have not yet been removed.

sentences.zh: 所謂九弊者，上有其六而下有其三：好勝人，恥聞過，騁辯給，眩聰明，厲威嚴，恣強愎，此六者，君上之弊也；

translations.literal: The so-called nine abuses: six belong to those above and three to those below — loving to surpass others, shaming to hear of faults, indulging in disputatious eloquence, dazzling with one's intelligence, imposing stern severity, giving free rein to obstinate willfulness — these six are the abuses of the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The so-called nine abuses are six on the ruler's side and three on the ministers' — loving to outdo others, shaming to hear of faults, indulging in glib argument, dazzling with one's cleverness, imposing harsh severity, and giving free rein to stubborn willfulness. These six are the ruler's abuses;

sentences.zh: 諂諛，顧望，畏心耎，此三者，臣下之弊也。

translations.literal: Flattery and sycophancy, looking to others and hesitating, a timid heart grown soft — these three are the abuses of officials below.
translations.idiomatic: flattery and sycophancy, looking to others and hesitating, and a timid heart grown soft. These three are the ministers' abuses.

sentences.zh: 上好勝必甘於佞辭，上恥過必忌於直諫，如是則下之諂諛者順旨而忠實之語不聞矣。

translations.literal: When the ruler loves to surpass others, he must delight in flattering words; when the ruler is shamed to hear of faults, he must be averse to straight remonstrance — thus flatterers below accord with his wishes and honest words are not heard.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler loves to outdo others, he must relish flattering words; when the ruler is shamed to hear of faults, he must loathe straight remonstrance. Then flatterers below will follow his wishes, and honest words will never be heard.

sentences.zh: 上騁辯必剿說而折人以言，上眩明必臆度而虞人以詐，如是則下之顧望者自便而切磨之辭不盡矣。

translations.literal: When the ruler indulges in disputatious eloquence, he must suppress discussion and refute people with words; when the ruler dazzles with intelligence, he must presume and suspect people of deceit — thus those below who look to others and hesitate take their own convenience and fully refined words are not fully expressed.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler indulges in argument, he must suppress debate and defeat people with words; when the ruler dazzles with cleverness, he must guess at motives and suspect people of deceit. Then those below who look to others and hesitate will take their own ease, and fully considered words will never be spoken.

sentences.zh: 上厲威必不能降情以接物，上恣愎必不能引咎以受規，如是則下之畏心耎者避辜而情理之說不申矣。

translations.literal: When the ruler imposes stern severity, he cannot lower his feelings to receive people; when the ruler gives free rein to obstinate willfulness, he cannot draw blame upon himself to accept regulation — thus those below with timid hearts grown soft avoid guilt and reasoned explanations are not made clear.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler imposes harsh severity, he cannot lower himself to receive people; when the ruler gives free rein to stubborn willfulness, he cannot accept blame and heed remonstrance. Then those below with timid hearts will avoid guilt, and reasoned counsel will never be fully expressed.

sentences.zh: 夫以區域之廣大，生靈之眾多，宮闕之重深，高卑之限隔，自黎獻而上，獲睹至尊之光景者，逾億兆而無一焉；

translations.literal: Considering the vastness of the territory, the multitude of the people, the depth and heaviness of the palace precincts, and the barrier of high and low rank — from the common folk upward, those who obtain a glimpse of the august presence exceed a hundred million yet not one in that number;
translations.idiomatic: Given the vastness of the realm, the multitude of the people, the depth of the palace precincts, and the barrier between high and low — from the common folk upward, those who even catch a glimpse of the Son of Heaven exceed a hundred million, yet not one in that number;

sentences.zh: 就獲睹之中得接言議者，又千萬不一；

translations.literal: Of those who obtain a glimpse, those who actually receive audience to speak on affairs are again one in ten million;
translations.idiomatic: of those who catch a glimpse, those who actually receive audience to speak on affairs are again one in ten million;

sentences.zh: 幸而得接者，猶有九弊居其間，則上下之情所通鮮矣。

translations.literal: Even those fortunate enough to receive audience still have the nine abuses standing between them — then what passes between the sentiments of above and below is scarce indeed.
translations.idiomatic: even those fortunate enough to receive audience still have the nine abuses standing between them — how little then passes between the feelings of above and below!

sentences.zh: 上情不通於下則人惑，下情不通於上則君疑。

translations.literal: When the sentiments of above do not reach below, people are confused; when the sentiments of below do not reach above, the ruler is suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler's feelings do not reach the people below, the people are confused; when the people's feelings do not reach the ruler above, the ruler grows suspicious.

sentences.zh: 疑則不納其誠，惑則不從其令。

translations.literal: Suspicious, he will not accept their sincerity; confused, they will not follow his commands.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicious, he will not accept their sincerity; confused, they will not obey his commands.

sentences.zh: 誠而不見納則應之以悖，令而不見從則加之以刑。

translations.literal: Sincerity not accepted is answered with defiance; commands not followed are reinforced with punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Sincerity not accepted is answered with defiance; commands not obeyed are answered with punishment.

sentences.zh: 下悖上刑，不敗何待！

translations.literal: Defiance below and punishment above — what need wait for ruin!
translations.idiomatic: Defiance below and punishment above — what need wait for ruin!

sentences.zh: 是使亂多理少，從古以然。」

translations.literal: This is what makes disorder many and order few — it has been so from antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: This is why disorder has always outnumbered order — it has been so from antiquity."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「昔趙武吶吶而為晉賢臣，絳侯木訥而為漢元輔。

translations.literal: Again: "In the past Zhao Wu was halting in speech yet became a worthy minister of Jin; the Marquis of Jiang was dull and slow-tongued yet became a chief minister of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He continued: "In the past Zhao Wu was halting in speech yet became a worthy minister of Jin; the Marquis of Jiang was dull and slow-tongued yet became a chief minister of Han.

sentences.zh: 然則口給者事或非信，辭屈者理或未窮。

translations.literal: Thus one glib of tongue — affairs may not be trustworthy; one whose words are defeated — principle may not be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Thus a glib tongue does not guarantee trustworthy counsel, and a defeated argument does not mean the reasoning is exhausted.

sentences.zh: 人之難知，堯、舜所病，胡可以一洲一詰而謂盡其能哉！

translations.literal: The difficulty of knowing people was what Yao and Shun took as their affliction — how can one inquiry and one questioning exhaust their abilities!
translations.idiomatic: The difficulty of knowing people was what even Yao and Shun found vexing — how can a single audience and a single challenge exhaust a man's abilities!

sentences.zh: 以此察天下之情，固多失實，以此輕天下之士，必有遺才。」

translations.literal: Using this to examine the sentiments of all under Heaven will certainly often miss the truth; using this to slight the scholars of all under Heaven will certainly leave talents behind."
translations.idiomatic: To judge the mood of the empire this way will often miss the truth; to slight the empire's men of talent this way will surely leave worthy men overlooked."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「諫者多，表我之能好；

translations.literal: Again: "When remonstrators are many, it shows my ability to welcome them;
translations.idiomatic: He added: "When remonstrators are many, it shows my willingness to welcome them;

sentences.zh: 諫者直，示我之能容；

translations.literal: when remonstrators are direct, it shows my ability to forbear;
translations.idiomatic: when remonstrators are blunt, it shows my capacity to forbear;

sentences.zh: 諫者之狂誣，明我之能恕；

translations.literal: when remonstrators are reckless and slanderous, it shows my ability to forgive;
translations.idiomatic: when remonstrators are reckless and slanderous, it shows my power to forgive;

sentences.zh: 諫者之漏洩，彰我之能從。

translations.literal: when remonstrators leak secrets, it manifests my ability to follow their counsel.
translations.idiomatic: when remonstrators leak secrets, it shows my willingness to follow their counsel.

sentences.zh: 有一於斯，皆為盛德。

translations.literal: To have any one of these is all great virtue.
translations.idiomatic: To possess any one of these is great virtue.

sentences.zh: 是則人君之與諫者交相益之道也。

translations.literal: This is the way in which the ruler and remonstrators mutually benefit each other.
translations.idiomatic: This is the way ruler and remonstrators mutually benefit each other.

sentences.zh: 諫者有爵賞之利，君亦有理安之利；

translations.literal: Remonstrators have the benefit of ranks and rewards; the ruler also has the benefit of order and peace.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators gain rank and reward; the ruler gains order and peace.

sentences.zh: 諫者得獻替之名，君亦得採納之名。

translations.literal: Remonstrators gain the reputation of offering advice for removal and replacement; the ruler also gains the reputation of selecting and accepting.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators win the name of offering candid counsel; the ruler wins the name of selecting and accepting it.

sentences.zh: 然猶諫者有失中而君無不美，唯恐讜言之不切，天下之不聞，如此則納諫之德光矣。」

translations.literal: Yet even when remonstrators miss the mark the ruler is wholly without blemish — only fearing that straight words are not cutting enough, that all under Heaven does not hear — thus the virtue of accepting remonstrance shines forth."
translations.idiomatic: Yet even when remonstrators miss the mark, the ruler remains without blemish — only fearing that straight words are not sharp enough and that all under Heaven does not hear them. Thus the virtue of accepting remonstrance shines forth."

sentences.zh: 上頗採用其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor took much of his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took much of his advice to heart.

sentences.zh: 李懷光頓兵不進，數上表暴揚盧杞等罪惡。

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang halted his army and did not advance; repeatedly submitted memorials loudly exposing the crimes of Lu Qi and others.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang halted his army and refused to advance, repeatedly submitting memorials that loudly exposed the crimes of Lu Qi and others.

sentences.zh: 眾論喧騰，亦咎杞等。

translations.literal: Public discussion boiled over; Lu Qi and others were also blamed.
translations.idiomatic: Public outcry swelled, and Lu Qi and the others were blamed as well.

sentences.zh: 上不得已，十二月，壬戌，貶杞為新州司馬，白志貞為恩州司馬，趙贊為播州司馬。

translations.literal: The Emperor had no choice; in the twelfth month, on the day renxu, demoted Lu Qi to Administrator of Xing Prefecture, Bai Zhizhen to Administrator of En Prefecture, and Zhao Zan to Administrator of Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no choice. In the twelfth month, on the day renxu, he demoted Lu Qi to Administrator of Xing Prefecture, Bai Zhizhen to Administrator of En Prefecture, and Zhao Zan to Administrator of Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宦者翟文秀，上所信任也，懷光又言其罪，上亦為殺之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Zhai Wenxiu, whom the Emperor trusted, Li Huaiguang also spoke of his crimes, and the Emperor had him killed as well.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Zhai Wenxiu, whom the emperor trusted, was also accused by Li Huaiguang; the emperor had him killed as well.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以翰林學士、祠部員外郎陸贄為考功郎中，金部員外郎吳通微為職方郎中。

translations.literal: On day yichou, appointed Hanlin Academician and Assistant Director of the Ministry of Rites Lu Zhi as Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and Assistant Director of the Ministry of Revenue Wu Tongwei as Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: On day yichou, the Hanlin Academician and Assistant Director of the Ministry of Rites Lu Zhi was appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and the Assistant Director of the Ministry of Revenue Wu Tongwei was appointed Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 贄上奏，辭以「初到奉天，扈從將吏例加兩階，今翰林獨遷官。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi submitted a memorial declining on the grounds: "When we first arrived at Fengtian, the generals and officers who accompanied Your Majesty were by precedent promoted two ranks; now the Hanlin alone receives a promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi submitted a memorial declining the appointment on the grounds that "when we first arrived at Fengtian, the generals and officers who accompanied Your Majesty were by precedent promoted two ranks, yet now the Hanlin alone receives a promotion.

sentences.zh: 夫行罰先貴近而後卑遠，則令不犯；

translations.literal: When inflicting punishment, start with the noble and near before the humble and far — then commands will not be violated;
translations.idiomatic: When punishment is applied first to the noble and near, then to the humble and far, commands will not be violated;

sentences.zh: 行賞先卑遠而後貴近，則功不遺。

translations.literal: when granting rewards, start with the humble and far before the noble and near — then merits will not be overlooked.
translations.idiomatic: when rewards are granted first to the humble and far, then to the noble and near, merit will not be overlooked.

sentences.zh: 望先錄大勞，次遍群品，則臣亦不敢獨辭。」

translations.literal: I hope the greatest services are recorded first, then rewards extended to all ranks in turn — then your servant also would not dare decline alone."
translations.idiomatic: I hope the greatest services are recorded first and rewards then extended to all ranks in turn — then your servant would not dare decline alone."

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 上在奉天，使人說田悅、王武俊、李納，赦其罪，厚賂以官爵。

translations.literal: While at Fengtian, the Emperor sent men to persuade Tian Yue, Wang Wujun, and Li Na, pardoning their crimes and lavishing them with rank and title as bribes.
translations.idiomatic: While at Fengtian, the emperor sent envoys to persuade Tian Yue, Wang Wujun, and Li Na, pardoning their crimes and lavishing them with rank and title.

sentences.zh: 悅等皆密歸款，而猶未敢絕朱滔，各稱王如故。

translations.literal: Tian Yue and the others all secretly pledged allegiance, yet still did not dare break with Zhu Tao; each continued to style himself king as before.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue and the others all secretly pledged allegiance, yet still did not dare break with Zhu Tao; each continued to style himself king as before.

sentences.zh: 滔使其虎牙將軍王郅說悅曰：「日者八郎有急，滔與趙王不敢愛其死，竭力赴救，幸而解圍。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao sent his Tiger-Fang General Wang Zhi to persuade Tian Yue, saying: "Recently when the Eighth Lord was in distress, Tao and the King of Zhao did not spare their lives, exerting all strength to rush to the rescue, and fortunately lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao sent his Tiger-Fang General Wang Zhi to persuade Tian Yue, saying: "Recently when the Eighth Lord was in distress, Tao and the King of Zhao did not spare their lives but exerted all their strength to rush to the rescue, and fortunately lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 今太尉三兄受命關中，滔欲與回紇共往助之，願八郎治兵，與滔渡河共取大梁。」

translations.literal: Now the Grand Marshal's third brother has received his commission in Guanzhong; Tao wishes to go with the Uyghurs to aid him. I hope the Eighth Lord will ready his troops and cross the river with Tao to jointly take Daliang."
translations.idiomatic: Now the Grand Marshal's third brother has received his commission in Guanzhong. Tao wishes to go with the Uyghurs to aid him. I hope the Eighth Lord will ready his troops and cross the river with Tao to take Daliang together."

sentences.zh: 悅心不欲行而未忍絕滔，乃許之。

translations.literal: Tian Yue did not wish to go in his heart yet could not bear to break with Zhu Tao, so he agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue did not wish to go in his heart yet could not bear to break with Zhu Tao, so he agreed.

sentences.zh: 滔復遣其內史舍人李琯見悅，審其可否，悅猶豫不決，密召扈崿等議之。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao again sent his Palace Secretariat Attendant Li Guan to see Tian Yue and ascertain whether he would go; Tian Yue hesitated and could not decide, secretly summoning Hu Yu and others to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao again sent his Palace Secretariat Attendant Li Guan to see Tian Yue and ascertain whether he would go. Tian Yue hesitated and could not decide, secretly summoning Hu Yu and others to discuss the matter.

sentences.zh: 司武侍郎許士則曰：「朱滔昔事李懷仙為牙將，與兄泚及朱希彩共殺懷仙而立希彩。

translations.literal: Vice Director of Martial Affairs Xu Shize said: "Zhu Tao once served Li Huaixian as a junior officer; with his elder brother Ci and Zhu Xicai he jointly killed Huaixian and enthroned Xicai.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of Martial Affairs Xu Shize said: "Zhu Tao once served Li Huaixian as a junior officer. With his elder brother Ci and Zhu Xicai he jointly killed Huaixian and enthroned Xicai.

sentences.zh: 希彩所以寵信其兄弟至矣，滔又與判官李子瑗謀殺希彩而立泚。

translations.literal: Xicai favored and trusted the brothers to the utmost, yet Tao again plotted with magistrate Li Ziyuan to kill Xicai and enthroned Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Xicai favored and trusted the brothers to the utmost, yet Tao again plotted with the magistrate Li Ziyuan to kill Xicai and enthroned Ci.

sentences.zh: 泚既為帥，滔乃勸泚入朝而自為留後，雖勸以忠義，實奪之權也。

translations.literal: Once Ci became commander, Tao urged Ci to enter court while taking the post of acting military governor himself — though urging loyalty and righteousness, in truth he seized his authority.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ci became commander, Tao urged Ci to enter court while taking the post of acting military governor himself — though urging loyalty and righteousness, in truth he seized Ci's authority.

sentences.zh: 平生與之同謀共功如李子瑗之徒，負而殺之者二十餘人。

translations.literal: Throughout his life, those who shared in plots and achievements with him such as Li Ziyuan — he betrayed and killed more than twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life, men who shared in plots and achievements with him, such as Li Ziyuan — he betrayed and killed more than twenty of them.

sentences.zh: 今又與泚東西相應，使滔得志，泚亦不為所容，況同盟乎！

translations.literal: Now he is again coordinating with Ci east and west; if Tao gets his way, even Ci will not be tolerated by him — how much less an alliance!
translations.idiomatic: Now he is again coordinating with Ci east and west. If Tao gets his way, even Ci will not be tolerated by him — how much less an ally!

sentences.zh: 滔為人如此。

translations.literal: Tao is such a man.
translations.idiomatic: This is the kind of man Tao is.

sentences.zh: 大王何從得其肺腑而信之邪！

translations.literal: Great King, how can you gain his inmost thoughts and trust him!
translations.idiomatic: Great King, how can you know his inmost heart and trust him!

sentences.zh: 彼引幽陵回紇十萬之兵屯於郊坰，大王出迎，則成擒矣。

translations.literal: If he leads a hundred thousand Uyghur troops from Youling to encamp in the outskirts, and the Great King goes out to welcome him, you will be captured outright.
translations.idiomatic: If he leads a hundred thousand Uyghur troops from Youling to encamp in the outskirts, and the Great King goes out to welcome him, you will be captured on the spot.

sentences.zh: 彼囚大王，兼魏國之兵，南向渡河，與關中相應，天下其孰能當之！

translations.literal: If he imprisons the Great King and takes the Wei state's army as well, crosses the river southward, and coordinates with Guanzhong — who in all under Heaven could withstand him!
translations.idiomatic: If he imprisons the Great King and takes the Wei army as well, crosses the river southward, and coordinates with Guanzhong — who in all under Heaven could withstand him!

sentences.zh: 大王於時悔之無及。

translations.literal: The Great King will then regret it when it is too late.
translations.idiomatic: The Great King will then regret it when it is too late.

sentences.zh: 為大王計，不若陽許偕行而陰為之備，厚加迎勞，至則托以它故，遣將分兵而隨之，如此，大王外不失報德之名而內無倉猝之憂矣。」

translations.literal: For the Great King's plan, it would be better to outwardly agree to go together while secretly preparing defenses — receive him with lavish welcome; when he arrives, plead some other reason, send generals with divided troops to follow him — thus the Great King outwardly loses no reputation for repaying kindness, and inwardly has no sudden alarm."
translations.idiomatic: For the Great King's plan, it would be better to outwardly agree to go together while secretly preparing defenses — receive him with lavish welcome, and when he arrives plead some other reason and send generals with divided troops to follow him. Thus the Great King outwardly keeps the name of repaying kindness, and inwardly has no sudden alarm."

sentences.zh: 扈崿等皆以為然。

translations.literal: Hu Yu and the others all considered this right.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yu and the others all agreed.

sentences.zh: 王武俊聞李琯適魏，遣其司刑員外郎田秀馳見悅曰：「武俊曏以宰相處事失宜，恐禍及身，又八郎困於重圍，故與滔合兵救之。

translations.literal: Wang Wujun heard Li Guan had arrived in Wei and sent his Assistant Director of Justice Tian Xiu in haste to see Tian Yue, saying: "Wujun, because the chief ministers handled affairs improperly and feared disaster reaching his person — and because the Eighth Lord was trapped in tight siege — therefore joined troops with Tao to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun heard that Li Guan had arrived in Wei and sent his Assistant Director of Justice Tian Xiu in haste to see Tian Yue, saying: "Wujun, because the chief ministers handled affairs improperly and feared disaster reaching his person — and because the Eighth Lord was trapped in tight siege — therefore joined troops with Tao to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 今天子方在隱憂，以德綏我，我曹何得不悔過而歸之邪！

translations.literal: Now the Son of Heaven is amid hidden sorrow, soothing us with virtue — how can we not repent our faults and return to him!
translations.idiomatic: Now the Son of Heaven is amid hidden sorrow, soothing us with virtue — how can we not repent our faults and return to him!

sentences.zh: 捨九葉天子不事而事泚及滔乎！

translations.literal: Abandon the Son of Heaven of nine generations and serve Ci and Tao instead!
translations.idiomatic: Abandon the Son of Heaven of nine generations and serve Ci and Tao instead!

sentences.zh: 且泚未稱帝之時，滔與我曹比肩為王，固已輕我曹矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, before Ci declared himself emperor, Tao stood shoulder to shoulder with us as kings — he already looked down on us.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, before Ci declared himself emperor, Tao stood shoulder to shoulder with us as kings — he already looked down on us.

sentences.zh: 況使之南平汴、洛，與泚連衡，吾屬皆為虜矣！

translations.literal: If he is allowed to pacify Bian and Luo in the south and link with Ci, we will all become captives!
translations.idiomatic: If he is allowed to pacify Bian and Luo in the south and link with Ci, we will all become captives!

sentences.zh: 八郎慎勿與之俱南，但閉城拒守。

translations.literal: Eighth Lord, be careful not to go south with him — only close the city and hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth Lord, be careful not to go south with him — only close the city and hold it.

sentences.zh: 武俊請伺其隙，連昭義之兵，擊而滅之，與八郎再清河朔，復為節度使，共事天子，不亦善乎！」

translations.literal: Wujun asks to watch for an opening, link with Zhao Yi's troops, strike and destroy him, and with the Eighth Lord again pacify the north, be restored as military governors, and serve the Son of Heaven together — would that not be fine!"
translations.idiomatic: Wujun asks to watch for an opening, link with Zhao Yi's troops, strike and destroy him, and with the Eighth Lord again pacify the north, be restored as military governors, and serve the Son of Heaven together — would that not be fine!"

sentences.zh: 悅意遂決，紿滔云：「從行，必如前約。」

translations.literal: Tian Yue's mind was then decided; he deceived Zhu Tao, saying: "I will go as agreed, just as in the former pact."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue's mind was then decided. He deceived Zhu Tao, saying: "I will go as agreed, just as in the former pact."

sentences.zh: 丁卯，滔將范陽步騎五萬人，私從者復萬餘人，回紇三千人，發河間而南，輜重首尾四十里。

translations.literal: On day dingmao, Zhu Tao led fifty thousand Fanyang infantry and cavalry, with more than ten thousand private followers besides, and three thousand Uyghurs, setting out from Hejian southward; supply wagons stretched forty li from head to tail.
translations.idiomatic: On day dingmao, Zhu Tao led fifty thousand Fanyang infantry and cavalry, with more than ten thousand private followers besides and three thousand Uyghurs, setting out from Hejian southward. Supply wagons stretched forty li from head to tail.

sentences.zh: 李希烈攻李勉於汴州，驅民運土木，築壘道，以攻城。

translations.literal: Li Xilie besieged Li Mian at Bian Prefecture, driving the people to transport earth and timber and build raised ramp-roads to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie besieged Li Mian at Bian Prefecture, driving the people to haul earth and timber and build raised ramp-roads to attack the city.

sentences.zh: 忿其未就，並人填之，謂之濕薪。

translations.literal: Angry that it was not finished, he buried people alive to fill it in — calling it "wet firewood."
translations.idiomatic: Angry that the work was not finished, he buried people alive to fill it in — calling it "wet firewood."

sentences.zh: 勉城守累月，外救不至，將其眾萬餘人奔宋州。

translations.literal: Li Mian defended the city for months; external relief did not arrive; he led his force of more than ten thousand and fled to Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian defended the city for months, but relief never came. He led his force of more than ten thousand and fled to Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庚午，希烈陷大梁。

translations.literal: On day gengwu, Li Xilie captured Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On day gengwu, Li Xilie captured Daliang.

sentences.zh: 滑州刺史李澄以城降希烈，希烈以澄為尚書令兼永平節度使。

translations.literal: Li Cheng, Prefect of Hua Prefecture, surrendered the city to Li Xilie; Li Xilie made Li Cheng Grand Counselor and concurrent Military Governor of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng, Prefect of Hua Prefecture, surrendered the city to Li Xilie. Li Xilie made Li Cheng Grand Counselor and concurrent Military Governor of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 勉上表請罪，上謂其使者曰：「朕猶失守宗廟，勉宜自安。」

translations.literal: Li Mian submitted a memorial requesting punishment; the Emperor told his envoy: "I myself have still lost the ancestral temple — Mian should set his mind at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian submitted a memorial requesting punishment. The emperor told his envoy: "I myself have still lost the ancestral temple — Mian should set his mind at ease."

sentences.zh: 待之如初。

translations.literal: He treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: He treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 劉洽遣其將高翼將精兵五千保襄邑，希烈攻拔之，翼赴水死。

translations.literal: Liu Qia sent his general Gao Yi with five thousand picked troops to hold Xiangyi; Li Xilie attacked and took it; Gao Yi threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qia sent his general Gao Yi with five thousand picked troops to hold Xiangyi. Li Xilie attacked and took it, and Gao Yi threw himself into the water and died.

sentences.zh: 希烈乘勝攻寧陵，江、淮大震。

translations.literal: Li Xilie pressed his victory to attack Ningling; the Jiang and Huai region was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie pressed his victory to attack Ningling, and the Jiang and Huai region was greatly shaken.

sentences.zh: 陳少游遣參謀溫述送款於希烈曰：「濠、壽、舒、廬，已令馳備，韜戈卷甲，伏俟指麾。」

translations.literal: Chen Shaoyou sent his staff officer Wen Shu to offer submission to Li Xilie, saying: "Hao, Shou, Shu, and Lu — I have already ordered swift preparations; weapons sheathed and armor rolled up, we wait concealed for your command."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou sent his staff officer Wen Shu to offer submission to Li Xilie, saying: "Hao, Shou, Shu, and Lu — I have already ordered swift preparations. Weapons are sheathed and armor rolled up; we wait concealed for your command."

sentences.zh: 又遣巡官趙詵結李納於鄆州。

translations.literal: He also sent touring officer Zhao Shen to connect with Li Na at Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent touring officer Zhao Shen to connect with Li Na at Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同平章事關播罷為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Equal to the Prime Minister Guan Bo was dismissed and made Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Equal to the Prime Minister Guan Bo was dismissed and made Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 以給事中孔巢父為淄青宣慰使，國子祭酒董晉為河北宣慰使。

translations.literal: Appointed Attendant of the Secretariat Kong Chaofu as Pacification Commissioner of Zi and Qing, and Chancellor of the Imperial Academy Dong Jin as Pacification Commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chaofu, Attendant of the Secretariat, was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Zi and Qing, and Dong Jin, Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 陸贄言於上曰：「今盜遍天下，輿駕播遷，陛下宜痛自引過以感人心。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi spoke to the Emperor, saying: "Now rebels fill all under Heaven and the imperial carriage has wandered in exile — Your Majesty should deeply blame yourself to move people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi spoke to the emperor, saying: "Now rebels fill the empire and the imperial carriage has wandered in exile. Your Majesty should deeply blame yourself to move people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 昔成湯以罪己勃興，楚昭以善言復國。

translations.literal: In the past Cheng Tang, by blaming himself, rose vigorously; King Zhao of Chu, through good words, restored his state.
translations.idiomatic: In the past King Tang of Shang, by blaming himself, rose vigorously; King Zhao of Chu, through good words, restored his state.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能不吝改過，以言射天下，使書詔開所避忌，臣雖愚陋，可以仰副聖情，庶令反側之徒革心向化。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly can be unstinting in correcting faults, speak forth to all under Heaven, and make written edicts open what has been taboo, your servant though dull and lowly can answer Your Majesty's sacred intent — perhaps making those who waver reform their hearts and turn toward transformation."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly can be unstinting in correcting faults, speak forth to all under Heaven, and make written edicts open what has been taboo, your servant though dull and lowly can answer Your Majesty's sacred intent — perhaps making those who waver reform their hearts and turn toward the throne."

sentences.zh: 上然之，故奉天所下書詔，雖驕將悍卒聞之，無不感激揮涕。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed; therefore the edicts issued from Fengtian — even proud generals and fierce soldiers, on hearing them, all were moved and wept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed. Therefore the edicts issued from Fengtian — even proud generals and fierce soldiers, on hearing them, all were moved and wept.

sentences.zh: 術者上言：「國家厄運，宜有變更以應時數。」

translations.literal: A diviner submitted a statement: "The state is in ill fortune; there should be changes to accord with the times and numbers."
translations.idiomatic: A diviner submitted a statement: "The state is in ill fortune; there should be changes to accord with the times and cosmic numbers."

sentences.zh: 群臣請更加尊號一二字。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers asked to add one or two characters to the honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers asked to add one or two characters to the honorific title.

sentences.zh: 上以問陸贄，贄上奏，以為不可，其略曰：「尊號之興，本非古制。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Lu Zhi; Lu Zhi submitted a memorial holding it impermissible, its gist running: "The rise of honorific titles is originally not an ancient institution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Lu Zhi. Lu Zhi submitted a memorial holding it impermissible, writing in essence: "The rise of honorific titles is originally not an ancient institution.

sentences.zh: 行於安泰之日，已累謙沖，襲乎喪亂之時，尤傷事體。」

translations.literal: Practiced in days of peace and security, it already strains modesty and restraint; carried on in times of calamity and disorder, it especially harms propriety."
translations.idiomatic: Practiced in days of peace and security, it already strains modesty and restraint; carried on in times of calamity and disorder, it especially harms propriety."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「贏秦德衰，兼皇與帝，始總稱之。

translations.literal: Again: "When the virtue of Qin declined, it combined 'emperor' and 'sovereign' and first used them as a general title.
translations.idiomatic: He continued: "When the virtue of Qin declined, it combined 'emperor' and 'sovereign' and first used them as a general title.

sentences.zh: 流及後代，昏僻之君，乃有聖劉、天元之號。

translations.literal: Flowing down to later generations, benighted and perverse rulers then had titles such as Holy Liu and Celestial Prime.
translations.idiomatic: Flowing down to later generations, benighted and perverse rulers then had titles such as Holy Liu and Celestial Prime.

sentences.zh: 是知人主輕重，不在名稱。

translations.literal: From this we know that the weight and dignity of a sovereign lord lie not in his titles.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that a ruler's true standing does not depend on his titles.

sentences.zh: 損之有謙光稽古之善，崇之獲矜能納諂之譏。」

translations.literal: To diminish them brings the virtue of modest radiance and consulting antiquity; to exalt them earns the reproach of taking pride in one's ability and welcoming flattery."
translations.idiomatic: To pare them back wins the praise of modesty and reverence for the past; to inflate them invites the charge of arrogance and a taste for sycophancy."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「必也俯稽術數，須有變更，與其增美稱而失人心，不若黜舊號以祗天戒。」

translations.literal: Again he said: "One must bow and examine numbers and portents — changes are required. Rather than add flattering titles and lose the people's hearts, it would be better to set aside the old designations to respect Heaven's warning."
translations.idiomatic: Again he said: "Your Majesty must look down and weigh the signs and reckonings of fate — change is needed. Better to retire the old titles and heed Heaven's warning than to pile on flattering epithets and lose the people's hearts."

sentences.zh: 上納其言，但改年號而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted his advice but changed only the era name.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took his counsel but changed only the era name.

sentences.zh: 上又以中書所撰赦文示贄，贄上言，以為：「動人以言，所感已淺，言又不切，人誰肯懷！

translations.literal: The Emperor also showed Lu Zhi the amnesty edict drafted by the Secretariat. Lu Zhi submitted a memorial, saying: "To move people with words already touches them but lightly; when the words are not pointed, who will take them to heart!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also showed Lu Zhi the amnesty edict drafted by the Secretariat. Lu Zhi submitted a memorial arguing that words alone move people only faintly, and when the words miss the mark, who will take them to heart?

sentences.zh: 今茲德音，悔過之意不得不深，引咎之辭不得不盡，洗刷疵垢，宣暢鬱堙，使人人各得所欲，則何有不從者乎！

translations.literal: In this gracious decree, the intent to repent must be inescapably deep, the language accepting blame inescapably complete — wash away stains and flaws, give full vent to pent-up grievances, so that every man obtains what he desires: then who would not follow!
translations.idiomatic: In this decree of grace, repentance must run deep and self-reproach must be spoken without reserve. Stains must be washed away and buried grievances aired, so that every man gets what he wants — then who would refuse to follow?

sentences.zh: 應須改革事條，謹具別狀同進。

translations.literal: Reforms to specific measures are required; I respectfully submit a separate memorial together with this one.
translations.idiomatic: Concrete reforms are needed; I respectfully submit a separate memorial along with this one.

sentences.zh: 捨此之外，尚有所虞。

translations.literal: Apart from this, there is still something to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this, I still have a concern.

sentences.zh: 竊以知過非難，改過為難；

translations.literal: Your servant holds that knowing one's faults is not hard, but reforming them is hard;
translations.idiomatic: I hold that knowing one's faults is not hard, but correcting them is;

sentences.zh: 言善非難，行善為難。

translations.literal: speaking what is good is not hard, but doing what is good is hard.
translations.idiomatic: speaking what is right is not hard, but doing what is right is.

sentences.zh: 假使赦文至精，止於知過言善，猶願聖慮更思所難。」

translations.literal: Even if the amnesty edict were perfectly crafted and stopped at knowing faults and speaking goodness, I would still wish Your Majesty's sacred deliberation to ponder further what is difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Even if the amnesty edict were perfectly worded and went no further than confessing fault and speaking virtue, I would still ask Your Majesty to weigh what is truly hard.

sentences.zh: 上然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝四興元元年（

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan of Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial and Sagely Cultural Emperor (
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan of Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial and Sagely Cultural Emperor (

sentences.zh: 甲子，公元七八四年）

translations.literal: Jiazi, AD 784)
translations.idiomatic: Jiazi, AD 784)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸酉朔，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the day guiyou, the first of the month, he granted amnesty throughout the realm and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guiyou, the new moon, he granted amnesty throughout the realm and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 制曰：「致理興化，必在推誠；

translations.literal: The edict said: "To bring order and raise culture, one must extend sincerity;
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "To govern well and renew the realm, one must act with sincerity;

sentences.zh: 忘己濟人，不吝改過。

translations.literal: forget oneself to benefit others, and not be sparing in reforming faults.
translations.idiomatic: forget oneself to serve others, and not shrink from correcting one's faults.

sentences.zh: 朕嗣服丕構，君臨萬邦，失守宗祧，越在草莽。

translations.literal: I have inherited the great enterprise and rule the myriad states, yet lost the ancestral temple and dwell in the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: I have inherited the great enterprise and rule the myriad states, yet I lost the ancestral temple and dwell in exile.

sentences.zh: 不念率德，誠莫追於既往；

translations.literal: Not mindful to lead by virtue — truly nothing can be recovered from what is past;
translations.idiomatic: I have not led by virtue, and the past cannot be undone;

sentences.zh: 永言思咎，期有復於將來。

translations.literal: ever speaking of reflecting on faults, I hope for restoration in what is to come.
translations.idiomatic: yet I will ever reflect on my faults and hope to make amends hereafter.

sentences.zh: 明征其義，以示天下。

translations.literal: I make clear its meaning to show it to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I proclaim this plainly to show it to all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 「小子懼德不嗣，罔敢怠荒，然以長於深宮之中，暗於經國之務，積習易溺，居安忘危，不知稼穡之艱難，不恤征戍之勞苦，澤靡下究，情未上通，事既擁隔，人懷疑阻。

translations.literal: "This unworthy son fears his virtue does not continue the line and dares not be idle or negligent; yet having grown up within the deep palace, I was dark to the business of governing the state. Habits piled up and were easy to sink into; dwelling in ease I forgot danger. I did not know the hardship of sowing and reaping, did not pity the toil of campaigning and garrison duty. Favor did not reach fully below; sentiment did not reach above. Affairs were blocked and separated, and people harbored doubt and obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: "This unworthy son fears his virtue does not match his inheritance and dares not be idle or negligent; yet I was raised in the deep palace and knew nothing of governing the realm. Old habits were easy to sink into; living in comfort I forgot danger. I did not know the hardship of the fields, nor pity the toil of campaign and garrison. Grace never reached the bottom; feeling never reached the top. Affairs piled up between us, and the people grew doubtful and estranged.

sentences.zh: 猶昧省己，遂用興戎，征師四方，轉餉千里，賦車籍馬，遠近騷然，行繼居送，眾庶勞止，或一日屢交鋒刃，或連年不解甲冑。

translations.literal: Still failing to examine myself, I then raised arms: armies were dispatched in every direction, supplies transported a thousand li, carts requisitioned and horses registered — near and far were thrown into turmoil. Those marching were followed by those staying behind to send them off; the multitude labored and halted. Some crossed blades many times in a single day; some went years without doffing armor.
translations.idiomatic: Still blind to my own faults, I raised arms. Armies marched in every direction; supplies moved a thousand li; carts were seized and horses registered — near and far were thrown into turmoil. Those who marched were followed by those who stayed behind to send them off; the people labored without rest. Some crossed blades many times in a single day; some went years without doffing armor.

sentences.zh: 祀奠乏主，室家靡依，死生流離，怨氣凝結，力役不息，田萊多荒。

translations.literal: Sacrifices and offerings lacked their masters; households had none to rely on. Life and death wandered in exile; resentment congealed and settled. Forced labor never ceased; fields and wasteland lay largely untilled.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices went unoffered; families lost their breadwinners. Life and death wandered in exile; resentment hardened into a mass. Forced labor never ceased; fields lay largely untilled.

sentences.zh: 暴令峻於誅求，疲□空於杼軸，轉死溝壑，離去鄉閭，邑裡丘墟，人煙斷絕。

translations.literal: Harsh commands were sharper than extortion; the exhausted populace was emptied at spindle and loom. People died in ditches and gullies; they left their villages and hamlets. Towns and hamlets became mounds and ruins; human smoke was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh orders outdid extortion; exhausted households were stripped to the spindle and loom. People died in ditches and gullies and fled their villages. Towns became ruins; the land grew empty of human smoke.

sentences.zh: 天譴於上而朕不寤，人怨於下而朕不知，馴致亂階，變興都邑，萬品失序，九廟震驚，上累於祖宗，下負於蒸庶，痛心靦貌，罪實在予，永言愧悼，若墜泉谷。

translations.literal: Heaven's reproach was above yet I did not awaken; the people's resentment was below yet I did not know. Step by step disorder arose; upheaval broke out in the capital. The myriad ranks lost order; the nine temples were shaken in alarm. Above I burdened the ancestors; below I failed the common people. My heart is pained and my face ashamed — the guilt is truly mine. Ever speaking of shame and grief, I am as if falling into a spring abyss.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven reproached me from above and I did not wake; the people resented me below and I did not know. Step by step disorder arose; rebellion broke out in the capital. All ranks lost their place; the ancestral temples were shaken. Above I shamed my forebears; below I failed the people. My heart aches and my face burns with shame — the guilt is truly mine. I am forever ashamed, as if falling into an abyss.

sentences.zh: 自今中外所上書奏，不得更言『聖神文武』之號。

translations.literal: From now on, memorials submitted within and without must no longer use the title 'Sagely, Divine, Martial, and Cultural.'
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth no memorial from within or without the court may again use the title 'Sagely, Divine, Martial, and Cultural.'

sentences.zh: 「李希烈、田悅、王武俊、李納等，鹹以勳舊，各守籓維，聯撫馭乖方，致其疑懼；

translations.literal: "Li Xilie, Tian Yue, Wang Wujun, Li Na, and the like — all men of merit and long service, each guarding a frontier domain — were governed and reassured by us in ways that missed the mark, causing their suspicion and fear;
translations.idiomatic: "Li Xilie, Tian Yue, Wang Wujun, Li Na, and the like — all men of merit and long service, each guarding a frontier domain — were governed by us in ways that missed the mark and drove them to suspicion and fear;

sentences.zh: 皆由上失其道而下罹其災，朕實不君，人則何罪！

translations.literal: all because those above lost the Way and those below suffered disaster. I truly failed as ruler — what crime have the people committed!
translations.idiomatic: all because the throne lost the Way and the people suffered for it. I alone failed as ruler — what crime have they committed!

sentences.zh: 宜並所管將吏等一切待之如初。

translations.literal: Their generals, officials, and the like under their command should all be treated as at first.
translations.idiomatic: All their generals, officials, and subordinates should be treated as before.

sentences.zh: 「朱滔雖緣朱泚連坐，路遠必不同謀，念其舊勳，務在弘貸，如能效順，亦與惟新。

translations.literal: "Though Zhu Tao was implicated by Zhu Ci's guilt by association, the distance makes joint plotting unlikely. Considering his old merit, we should aim at broad clemency; if he can submit and turn loyal, he too shall share in renewal.
translations.idiomatic: "Though Zhu Tao was implicated through Zhu Ci's guilt, the distance between them makes joint plotting unlikely. In view of his old service, we should show broad clemency; if he submits and turns loyal, he too shall share in this renewal.

sentences.zh: 「朱泚反易天常，盜竊名器，暴犯陵寢，所不忍言，獲罪祖宗，朕不敢赦。

translations.literal: "Zhu Ci reversed Heaven's constant order, stole the regalia of office, and violently violated the imperial tombs — what I cannot bear to speak of. Having offended the ancestors, I dare not pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: "Zhu Ci overturned Heaven's order, stole the symbols of rule, and violently violated the imperial tombs — what I cannot bear to put into words. Having offended the ancestors, I dare not pardon him.

sentences.zh: 其脅從將吏百姓等，但官軍未到京城以前，去逆效順並散歸本道、本軍者，並從赦例。

translations.literal: Among the generals, officials, common people, and the like who were coerced to follow him — provided only that before the imperial army reached the capital they left rebellion, submitted, and dispersed back to their original circuits and armies — all shall come under the amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: As for the generals, officials, and common people who followed under duress — if before the imperial army reached the capital they abandoned rebellion, submitted, and returned to their own circuits and armies — all shall be covered by the amnesty.

sentences.zh: 「諸軍、諸道應赴奉天及進收京城將士，並賜名奉天定難功臣。

translations.literal: "All armies and all circuits whose officers and soldiers answered the call to Fengtian and advanced to recover the capital shall be granted the name Fengtian Dingnan Meritorious Servants.
translations.idiomatic: "All armies and circuits whose troops marched to Fengtian and helped recover the capital shall be granted the title Meritorious Servants Who Settled the Crisis at Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 其所加墊陌錢、稅間架、竹、木、茶、漆、榷鐵之類，悉宜停罷。」

translations.literal: The added dianmo cash, the jianjia housing tax, taxes on bamboo, timber, tea, lacquer, iron monopolies, and the like — all should be halted and abolished."
translations.idiomatic: The added dianmo levy, the jianjia housing tax, and taxes on bamboo, timber, tea, lacquer, and iron monopolies — all such imposts shall be abolished."

sentences.zh: 赦下，四方人心大悅。

translations.literal: When the amnesty was promulgated, hearts throughout the four quarters were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the amnesty was promulgated, people throughout the realm rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 及上還長安明年，李抱真入朝為上言：「山東宣佈赦書，士卒皆感泣，臣見人情如此，知賊不足平也！」

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned to Chang'an the following year, Li Baozhen came to court and said to him: "When the amnesty edict was proclaimed in Shandong, the soldiers all wept with emotion. Your servant saw sentiment like this and knew the rebels could not long stand!"
translations.idiomatic: The year after the Emperor returned to Chang'an, Li Baozhen came to court and said, "When the amnesty was proclaimed in the east, the soldiers wept with emotion. When I saw feeling like that, I knew the rebels could not long stand!"

sentences.zh: 命兵部員外郎李充為恆冀宣慰使。

translations.literal: Li Chong, vice director in the Ministry of War, was appointed pacification commissioner for Heng and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, vice director in the Ministry of War, was appointed pacification commissioner for Heng and Ji.

sentences.zh: 朱泚更國號曰漢，自稱漢元天皇，改元天皇。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci changed the state name to Han, styled himself Han Yuan Heavenly Emperor, and changed the era name to Tianhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci changed the state name to Han, styled himself Han Yuan Heavenly Emperor, and adopted the era name Tianhuang.

sentences.zh: 王武俊、田悅、李納見赦令，皆去王號，上表謝罪。

translations.literal: Wang Wujun, Tian Yue, and Li Na, on seeing the amnesty edict, all relinquished their royal titles and submitted memorials asking pardon.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Wujun, Tian Yue, and Li Na saw the amnesty edict, they all dropped their royal titles and submitted memorials asking pardon.

sentences.zh: 惟李希烈自恃兵強財富，遂謀稱帝，遣人問儀於顏真卿，真卿曰：「老夫嘗為禮官，所記惟諸侯朝天子禮耳！」

translations.literal: Only Li Xilie, trusting in his strong armies and rich stores, then plotted to declare himself emperor. He sent men to ask Yan Zhenqing about the rites. Zhenqing said: "This old man once served as a ritual official; what I remember is only the rites for feudal lords attending upon the Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Only Li Xilie, trusting in his strong armies and rich stores, plotted to declare himself emperor. He sent men to ask Yan Zhenqing about the rites. Zhenqing replied, "This old man once served as a ritual official; all I remember are the rites for feudal lords attending upon the Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 希烈遂即皇帝位，國號大楚，改元武成。

translations.literal: Xilie thereupon assumed the imperial throne, named his state Great Chu, and changed the era name to Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie thereupon took the imperial throne, named his state Great Chu, and adopted the era name Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 置百官，以其黨鄭賁為侍中，孫廣為中書令，李緩、李元平同平章事。

translations.literal: He established the full bureaucracy, appointing his partisan Zheng Ben as Palace Attendant, Sun Guang as Director of the Secretariat, and Li Huan and Li Yuanping as co-directors of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He established a full bureaucracy, appointing his partisan Zheng Ben as Palace Attendant, Sun Guang as Director of the Secretariat, and Li Huan and Li Yuanping as co-directors of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以汴州為在梁府，分其境內為四節度。

translations.literal: He made Bian Prefecture his capital at Liang and divided his territory into four military governorships.
translations.idiomatic: He made Bian Prefecture his capital at Liang and divided his territory into four military governorships.

sentences.zh: 希烈遣其將辛景臻謂顏真卿曰：「不能屈節，當自焚！」

translations.literal: Xilie sent his general Xin Jingzhen to say to Yan Zhenqing: "If you cannot bend your integrity, you should burn yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Xilie sent his general Xin Jingzhen to tell Yan Zhenqing, "If you will not submit, burn yourself!"

sentences.zh: 積薪灌油於其庭。

translations.literal: They piled firewood in his courtyard and poured oil over it.
translations.idiomatic: They piled firewood in his courtyard and poured oil over it.

sentences.zh: 真卿趨赴火，景臻遽止之。

translations.literal: Zhenqing rushed toward the fire; Jingzhen hastily stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing rushed toward the flames; Jingzhen hastily stopped him.

sentences.zh: 希烈又遣其將楊峰繼赦賜陳少游及壽州刺史張建封。

translations.literal: Xilie also sent his general Yang Feng to follow up the amnesty gifts to Chen Shaoyou and Zhang Jianfeng, prefect of Shou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie also sent his general Yang Feng to deliver follow-up amnesty gifts to Chen Shaoyou and Zhang Jianfeng, prefect of Shou.

sentences.zh: 建封執峰徇於軍，腰斬於市，少游聞之駭懼。

translations.literal: Jianfeng seized Feng, paraded him before the army, and had him beheaded at the waist in the marketplace. Shaoyou, hearing of it, was struck with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng seized Feng, paraded him before the army, and had him cut in two at the waist in the marketplace. When Shaoyou heard of it, he was terrified.

sentences.zh: 建封具以少游與希烈交通之狀聞，上悅，以建封為濠、壽、廬三州都團練使。

translations.literal: Jianfeng reported in full Chen Shaoyou's communications with Xilie. The Emperor was pleased and appointed Jianfeng overall training commissioner of Hao, Shou, and Lu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng reported in full Chen Shaoyou's dealings with Xilie. The Emperor was pleased and appointed Jianfeng overall training commissioner of Hao, Shou, and Lu.

sentences.zh: 希烈乃以其將杜少誠為淮南節度使，使將步騎萬餘人先取壽州，後之江都，建封遣其將賀蘭元均、邵怡守霍丘秋柵。

translations.literal: Xilie then made his general Du Shaoqian military governor of Huainan and sent him with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry first to take Shou Prefecture and then advance to Jiangdu. Jianfeng sent his generals Helan Yuanjun and Shao Yi to hold the Qiuchai stockade at Huoqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie then made his general Du Shaoqian military governor of Huainan and sent him with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to take Shou first and then advance on Jiangdu. Jianfeng sent his generals Helan Yuanjun and Shao Yi to hold the Qiuchai stockade at Huoqiu.

sentences.zh: 少誠竟不能過，遂南寇蘄、黃，欲斷江路，時上命包佶自督江、淮財賦，溯江詣行在。

translations.literal: Shaoqian in the end could not get through, so he raided south into Qi and Huang, intending to cut the Yangzi route. At that time the Emperor ordered Bao Ji to supervise Jiang-Huai revenues himself and sail upriver to the temporary court.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqian could not break through, so he raided south into Qi and Huang, intending to cut the Yangzi route. The Emperor had ordered Bao Ji to supervise Jiang-Huai revenues himself and sail upriver to the temporary court.

sentences.zh: 至蘄口，遇少誠入寇。

translations.literal: When he reached Qikou, he encountered Shaoqian raiding in.
translations.idiomatic: At Qikou he ran into Shaoqian's raiding force.

sentences.zh: 曹王皋遣蘄州刺史伊慎將兵七千拒之，戰於永安戍，大破之，少誠脫身走，斬首萬級，包佶乃得前。

translations.literal: Prince Cao Wang Gao sent Yi Shen, prefect of Qi, with seven thousand troops to resist him. They fought at Yong'an garrison and routed the enemy decisively. Shaoqian escaped with his life; ten thousand heads were taken. Bao Ji was then able to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cao Wang Gao sent Yi Shen, prefect of Qi, with seven thousand men to block him. They fought at Yong'an garrison and won a great victory. Shaoqian escaped; ten thousand heads were taken. Bao Ji was then able to continue.

sentences.zh: 後佶入朝，具奏陳少游奪財賦事。

translations.literal: Later, when Ji came to court, he memorialized in full Chen Shaoyou's seizure of revenues.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Bao Ji came to court, he memorialized in full on Chen Shaoyou's seizure of revenues.

sentences.zh: 少游懼，厚斂所部以償之。

translations.literal: Shaoyou was afraid and levied heavily on his jurisdiction to repay it.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou was afraid and levied heavily on his jurisdiction to make restitution.

sentences.zh: 李希烈以夏口上流要地，使其驍將董侍募死士七千人襲鄂州，刺史李兼偃旗臥鼓閉門以待之。

translations.literal: Li Xilie, because Xiakou was a key point on the upper reaches, sent his fierce general Dong Shi to recruit seven thousand death-defying men to strike E Prefecture. Prefect Li Jian lowered banners, stilled drums, and shut the gates to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiakou was a key point on the upper Yangzi, Li Xilie sent his fierce general Dong Shi to raise seven thousand death-defying men and strike E Prefecture. Prefect Li Jian lowered his banners, stilled his drums, and shut the gates to await them.

sentences.zh: 侍撤屋材以焚門，兼帥士卒出戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Shi tore up house timbers to burn the gate; Jian led his soldiers out to fight and routed them decisively.
translations.idiomatic: Shi tore up house timbers to burn the gate; Jian led his troops out and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 上以兼為鄂、岳、沔都團練使。

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed Jian overall training commissioner of E, Yue, and Mian.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor appointed Li Jian overall training commissioner of E, Yue, and Mian.

sentences.zh: 於是希烈東畏曹王皋，西畏李兼，不敢復有窺江、淮之志矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xilie feared Prince Cao Wang Gao in the east and Li Jian in the west, and no longer dared harbor designs on the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Xilie feared Prince Cao Wang Gao in the east and Li Jian in the west, and no longer dared cast covetous eyes on the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 朱滔引兵入趙境，王武俊大具犒享。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao led his army into Zhao territory; Wang Wujun lavishly prepared feasts and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao led his army into Zhao territory; Wang Wujun prepared lavish feasts and rewards.

sentences.zh: 入魏境，田悅供承倍豐，使者迎候，相望於道。

translations.literal: Entering Wei territory, Tian Yue supplied and received him twice as generously; envoys greeted and attended him, one after another along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Wei territory, Tian Yue supplied him twice as generously as before; envoys greeted him one after another all along the road.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，滔至永濟，遣王郅見悅，約會館陶，偕行渡河。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, Tao reached Yongji and sent Wang Zhi to see Yue, arranging to meet at Guantao and cross the river together.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Tao reached Yongji and sent Wang Zhi to see Yue, arranging to meet at Guantao and cross the river together.

sentences.zh: 悅見郅曰：「悅固願從五兄南行，昨日將出軍，將士勒兵不聽悅出，曰：國兵新破，戰守逾年，資儲竭矣。

translations.literal: Yue, seeing Zhi, said: "Yue has indeed wished to follow Fifth Brother south. Yesterday, when I was about to lead the army out, the officers and soldiers restrained their arms and would not let Yue go out, saying: 'The imperial army was just defeated; we have fought and held out for more than a year, and stores are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Yue told Zhi, "I truly wish to follow Fifth Brother south. Yesterday, when I was about to march out, my officers and soldiers drew up their arms and refused to let me go, saying, 'The imperial army was just beaten; we have fought and held out for more than a year, and our stores are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 今將士不免凍餒，何以全軍遠征！

translations.literal: Now the officers and soldiers cannot escape cold and hunger — how can the whole army make a distant expedition!
translations.idiomatic: Now the men cannot escape cold and hunger — how can the whole army march on a distant campaign!

sentences.zh: 大王日自撫循，猶不能安，若捨城邑而去，朝出，暮必有變！』

translations.literal: Great King personally soothes and reassures them day by day and still cannot settle them. If you abandon the cities and depart, go out in the morning and by evening there will surely be upheaval!'"
translations.idiomatic: Great King soothes them day by day and still cannot settle them. If you abandon the cities and leave, march out in the morning and by evening there will surely be trouble!'"

sentences.zh: 悅之志非敢有貳也，如將士何！

translations.literal: Yue's intent does not dare to be double-minded — but what can be done about the officers and soldiers!
translations.idiomatic: My heart is not divided — but what can I do about the officers and soldiers!

sentences.zh: 已令孟祐備步騎五千，從五兄供芻牧之役。」

translations.literal: I have already ordered Meng You to prepare five thousand infantry and cavalry to follow Fifth Brother and supply fodder and grazing duties."
translations.idiomatic: I have already ordered Meng You to prepare five thousand infantry and cavalry to follow Fifth Brother and supply fodder and grazing duties.

sentences.zh: 因遣其司禮侍郎裴抗等往謝滔。

translations.literal: He then sent his Director of Ritual Pei Kang and others to apologize to Tao.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his Director of Ritual Pei Kang and others to apologize to Tao.

sentences.zh: 滔聞之，大怒曰：「田悅逆賊，曏在重圍，命如絲發，使我叛君棄兄，發兵晝夜赴之，幸而得存。

translations.literal: When Tao heard this, he flew into a rage and said: "Tian Yue, rebellious bandit — lately trapped in heavy siege, his life hanging by a thread — made me betray my lord and abandon my elder brother, dispatching troops day and night to his aid, and by good fortune he survived.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao heard this, he flew into a rage and said, "Tian Yue, that rebel — when he was trapped in heavy siege with his life hanging by a thread, he made me betray my lord and abandon my elder brother and march day and night to save him. By good fortune he survived.

sentences.zh: 許我貝州，我辭不取；

translations.literal: He offered me Bei Prefecture and I declined to take it;
translations.idiomatic: He offered me Bei Prefecture and I refused it;

sentences.zh: 尊我為天子，我辭不受，今乃負恩，誤我遠來，飾辭不出！」

translations.literal: he honored me as Son of Heaven and I declined to accept — yet now he fails in gratitude, has misled me into coming from afar, and dresses up excuses not to march out!"
translations.idiomatic: he wanted to make me Son of Heaven and I refused — yet now he repays kindness with betrayal, lured me here from afar, and hides behind polished excuses not to march out!"

sentences.zh: 即日，遣馬寔攻宗城、經城，楊榮國攻冠氏，皆拔之。

translations.literal: That same day he sent Ma Shi to attack Zongcheng and Jingcheng, and Yang Rongguo to attack Guanshi — all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he sent Ma Shi to attack Zongcheng and Jingcheng, and Yang Rongguo to attack Guanshi — all were taken.

sentences.zh: 又縱回紇掠館陶頓幄帟、器皿、車、牛以去。

translations.literal: He also let the Uighurs plunder Guantao of tent curtains, utensils, carts, and oxen and depart.
translations.idiomatic: He also let the Uighurs plunder Guantao of tents, utensils, carts, and oxen and depart.

sentences.zh: 悅閉城自守。

translations.literal: Yue shut the city and held it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yue shut himself inside the city and held out.

sentences.zh: 壬午，滔遣裴抗等還，分兵置吏守平恩、永濟。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, Tao sent Pei Kang and the others back, divided his troops, and placed officials to hold Ping'en and Yongji.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Tao sent Pei Kang and the others back, divided his troops, and posted officials to hold Ping'en and Yongji.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以吏部侍郎盧翰為兵部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, Lu Han, vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, was made vice director in the Ministry of War and co-director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Lu Han, vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, was made vice director in the Ministry of War and co-director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 翰，義僖之七世孫也。

translations.literal: Han was the seventh-generation descendant of Lu Yixi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Han was the seventh-generation descendant of Lu Yixi.

sentences.zh: 朱滔引兵北圍貝州，引水環之，刺史刑曹俊嬰城拒守。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao led his army north to besiege Bei Prefecture, drew water to ring it, and Prefect Xing Caojun closed the city and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao led his army north to besiege Bei Prefecture, drew water to ring the city, and Prefect Xing Caojun shut the gates and held out.

sentences.zh: 縱范陽及回紇兵大掠諸縣，又拔武城，通德、棣二州，使給軍食。

translations.literal: He let the Fanyang and Uighur troops plunder the counties on a large scale, also took Wucheng, and opened communications with De and Di prefectures to supply army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He let the Fanyang and Uighur troops plunder the counties, also took Wucheng, and opened communications with De and Di to supply his army.

sentences.zh: 遣馬寔將步騎五千屯冠氏以逼魏州。

translations.literal: He sent Ma Shi with five thousand infantry and cavalry to encamp at Guanshi to press Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Ma Shi with five thousand infantry and cavalry to encamp at Guanshi and press Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以給事中杜黃裳為江淮宣慰副使。

translations.literal: Du Huangshang, attendant within the Secretariat, was made deputy pacification commissioner for Jiang-Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huangshang, attendant within the Secretariat, was made deputy pacification commissioner for Jiang-Huai.

sentences.zh: 上於行宮廡下貯諸道貢獻之物，榜曰瓊林大盈庫。

translations.literal: At the temporary palace the Emperor stored the tribute gifts from the various circuits beneath the corridor eaves and posted a sign reading Qionglinda Ying Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: At the temporary palace the Emperor stored tribute gifts from the various circuits beneath the corridor eaves and posted a sign naming the treasury Qionglinda Ying.

sentences.zh: 陸贄以為戰守之功，賞賚未行而遽私別庫，則士卒怨望，無復鬥志，上疏諫，其略曰：「天子與天同德，以四海為家，何必橈廢公方，崇聚私貨！

translations.literal: Lu Zhi held that after the merit of fighting and holding the city, rewards had not yet been granted yet a separate private treasury was hastily set up — then the soldiers would resent and lose fighting spirit. He submitted a remonstrance, the gist of which ran: "The Son of Heaven shares virtue with Heaven and takes the four seas as his home — why must public rectitude be bent aside and private goods heaped up!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi argued that after the merit of fighting and holding the city, rewards had not yet been granted yet the Emperor had hastily set aside a private treasury — the soldiers would resent it and lose their fighting spirit. He submitted a remonstrance, the gist of which ran: "The Son of Heaven shares virtue with Heaven and takes the four seas as his home — why bend public rectitude aside and heap up private goods!

sentences.zh: 降至尊而代有司之守，辱萬乘以效匹夫之藏，虧法失人，誘姦聚怨，以斯制事，豈不過哉！」

translations.literal: To lower the supreme lord and stand in for the officials charged with their duties, to disgrace the chariot of ten thousand teams in imitating a common man's hoard — this injures the law, loses the people, invites wickedness, and gathers resentment. To govern affairs thus — is it not excessive!"
translations.idiomatic: To lower the supreme lord and do the work of petty officials, to disgrace the imperial chariot by imitating a common man's hoard — this injures the law, loses the people, invites wickedness, and gathers resentment. To govern this way — is it not going too far!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「頃者六師初降，百物無儲，外扞兇徒，內防危堞，晝夜不息，迨將五旬，凍餒交侵，死傷相枕，畢命同力，竟夷大艱。

translations.literal: Again he said: "Recently, when the six armies first submitted, there were stores of nothing; outwardly they held off violent bands, inwardly they defended perilous walls — day and night without rest, nearly fifty days. Cold and hunger pressed together; dead and wounded lay one upon another. They gave their lives with united strength and finally levelled the great crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Again he said: "Recently, when the six armies first submitted, we had nothing in store; outwardly they held off the rebels, inwardly they defended the walls — day and night without rest for nearly fifty days. Cold and hunger pressed in together; dead and wounded lay one upon another. They gave their lives with one accord and finally overcame the great crisis.

sentences.zh: 良以陛下不厚其身，不私其欲，絕甘以同卒伍，輟食以啖功勞。

translations.literal: Truly it was because Your Majesty did not enrich himself, did not indulge his desires, renounced delicacies to share with the ranks, and stopped his own food to feed those who had labored.
translations.idiomatic: Truly it was because Your Majesty did not enrich himself or indulge his desires — you renounced delicacies to share with the ranks and stopped your own meals to feed those who had labored.

sentences.zh: 無猛制而人不攜，懷所感也；

translations.literal: Without harsh control the people did not desert — they cherished what they felt;
translations.idiomatic: Without harsh control the men did not desert — they were moved by what they felt;

sentences.zh: 無厚賞而人不怨，悉所無也。

translations.literal: without rich rewards the people did not resent — because you had nothing to give.
translations.idiomatic: without rich rewards the men did not resent — because you had nothing to give.

sentences.zh: 今者攻圍已解，衣食已豐，而謠讟方興，軍情稍阻，豈不以勇夫恆性，嗜利矜功，其患難既與之同憂，而好樂不與之同利，苟異恬默，能無怨咨！」

translations.literal: Now the siege is lifted and clothing and food are plentiful, yet slander is rising and army sentiment is somewhat blocked — is it not because brave men by nature love profit and prize merit? They shared hardship and worry with you, yet good fortune and pleasure are not shared with them in profit. If things differ and they keep silent, how can there be no resentment and complaint!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the siege is lifted and clothing and food are plentiful, yet grumbling is rising and army morale is faltering — is it not because brave men by nature love profit and prize merit? They shared hardship with you, yet good fortune is not shared with them. How can they keep silent and not complain!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「陛下誠能近想重圍之殷憂，追戒平居之專欲，凡在二庫貨賄，盡令出賜有功，每獲珍華，先給軍賞，如此，則亂必靖，賊必平，徐駕六龍，旋復都邑，天子之貴，豈當憂貧！

translations.literal: Again he said: "If Your Majesty can truly recall the deep anxiety of heavy siege close at hand and take warning from ordinary days of exclusive desire — let all goods and bribes in the two treasuries be issued as gifts to those with merit; whenever rare treasures are obtained, give army rewards first — then disorder will surely be settled, rebels will surely be pacified, and slowly driving the six dragons you will return to the capital. The Son of Heaven's dignity — how should he worry about poverty!
translations.idiomatic: Again he said: "If Your Majesty can truly recall the deep anxiety of the siege and take warning from ordinary days of selfish desire — let all goods in the two treasuries be issued as gifts to those with merit; whenever rare treasures arrive, give army rewards first — then disorder will be settled, rebels will be pacified, and slowly driving the six dragons you will return to the capital. The Son of Heaven's dignity — why should he worry about poverty!

sentences.zh: 是乃散其小儲而成其大儲，損其小寶而固其大寶也。」

translations.literal: This is to scatter the small store and complete the great store, diminish the small treasure and secure the great treasure."
translations.idiomatic: That is to scatter a small hoard and build a great one, to spend a small treasure and secure a great treasure."

sentences.zh: 上即命去其榜。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately ordered the sign removed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor immediately ordered the sign removed.

sentences.zh: 蕭復嘗言於上曰：「宦官自艱難以來，多為監軍，恃恩縱橫。

translations.literal: Xiao Fu once said to the Emperor: "Since the crisis, eunuchs have often served as army supervisors, relying on favor to run rampant.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fu once told the Emperor, "Since the crisis, eunuchs have often served as army supervisors, relying on favor to run rampant.

sentences.zh: 此屬但應掌宮掖之事，不宜委以兵權國政。」

translations.literal: These men should only manage affairs of the palace inner quarters; they should not be entrusted with military authority and state governance."
translations.idiomatic: These men should manage only palace affairs; they should not be entrusted with military authority or state governance.

sentences.zh: 上不悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 又嘗言：「陛下踐祚之初，聖德光被，自用楊炎、盧杞黷亂朝政，以致今日。

translations.literal: He also once said: "When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, sagely virtue shone everywhere; then by your own choice Yang Yan and Lu Qi profaned and disordered court governance, leading to today.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, your virtue shone everywhere; then by your own choice Yang Yan and Lu Qi corrupted court governance and brought us to this day.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能變更睿志，臣敢不竭力？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty will truly change your sagely resolve, how would your servant dare not exert his utmost strength?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will truly change your mind, how could I fail to give you my full strength?

sentences.zh: 倘使臣依阿苟免，臣實不能。」

translations.literal: If your servant were to fawn and seek only to escape blame, your servant truly could not do it."
translations.idiomatic: But if you expect me to flatter and dodge blame, I truly cannot."

sentences.zh: 又嘗與盧杞同奏事，杞順上旨，復正色曰：「盧杞言不正！」

translations.literal: He also once memorialized together with Lu Qi; Qi followed the emperor's intent, but Fu sternly said: "What Lu Qi says is not correct!"
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he memorialized alongside Lu Qi. Qi spoke to please the emperor, but Xiao Fu said sternly, "Lu Qi is wrong!"

sentences.zh: 上愕然，退，謂左右曰：「蕭復輕朕！」

translations.literal: The emperor was startled; afterward he withdrew and said to those beside him: "Xiao Fu looks down on me!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled. After the audience he told his attendants, "Xiao Fu disrespects me!"

sentences.zh: 戊子，命復棄山南東、西、荊湖、淮南、江西、鄂岳、浙江東、西、福建、嶺南等道宣慰、安撫使，實疏之也。

translations.literal: On wuzi he ordered Fu to relinquish the posts of pacification and consolation commissioner for Shannan East and West, Jinghu, Huainan, Jiangxi, E-Yue, Zhejiang East and West, Fujian, Lingnan, and other circuits — in truth to distance him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuzi he stripped Fu of his appointment as pacification commissioner over Shannan, Jinghu, Huainan, Jiangxi, E-Yue, the two Zhejiangs, Fujian, Lingnan, and the other southern circuits — in effect pushing him aside.

sentences.zh: 既而劉從一及朝士往往奏留復，上謂陸贄曰：「朕思遷幸以來，江、淮遠方，或傳聞過實，欲遣重臣宣慰，謀於宰相及朝士，僉謂宜然。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Liu Congyi and court officials repeatedly memorialized to keep Fu; the emperor said to Lu Zhi: "Since the move of the court, in the distant Jiang-Huai regions rumors may have exceeded fact; I wished to send a senior minister to proclaim reassurance. I consulted the chief ministers and court officials, and all said it should be done.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liu Congyi and other officials memorialized repeatedly asking Fu to stay. The emperor told Lu Zhi, "Since we fled the capital, distant regions along the Yangzi may have heard exaggerated rumors. I wanted to send a senior minister to reassure them. I consulted the chief ministers and the court, and everyone agreed.

sentences.zh: 今乃反覆如是，朕為之悵恨累日。

translations.literal: Now it turns back and forth like this — I have brooded over it in regret for many days.
translations.idiomatic: Now matters have reversed themselves like this, and I have brooded over it in regret for days.

sentences.zh: 意復悔行，使之論奏邪？

translations.literal: Do you think Fu regrets going and had them memorialize on his behalf?
translations.idiomatic: Do you think Fu changed his mind and had them petition for him?

sentences.zh: 卿知蕭復如何人？

translations.literal: Do you know what sort of man Xiao Fu is?
translations.idiomatic: What sort of man is Xiao Fu, in your view?

sentences.zh: 其不欲行，意趣安在？」

translations.literal: If he did not wish to go, what was his intent?"
translations.idiomatic: If he did not want to go, what was he after?"

sentences.zh: 贄上奏，以為：「復痛自修勵，慕為清貞，用雖不周，行則可保。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized, holding: "Fu disciplines himself sternly and aspires to integrity; though his usefulness may not be comprehensive, his conduct can be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi replied that Fu was strict with himself and aspired to integrity — his talents might not cover every need, but his conduct could be trusted.

sentences.zh: 至於輕詐如此，復必不為。

translations.literal: As for being so lightly deceitful, Fu would certainly not do it.
translations.idiomatic: As for playing such petty tricks, Fu would never do that.

sentences.zh: 借使復欲逗留，從一安肯附會！

translations.literal: Even if Fu wished to linger, how would Congyi be willing to collude!
translations.idiomatic: Even if Fu wanted to stay, why would Liu Congyi collude with him!

sentences.zh: 今所言矛楯，願陛下明加辯詰。

translations.literal: What is said now is contradictory; I ask Your Majesty clearly to question and examine it.
translations.idiomatic: The stories contradict each other. I urge Your Majesty to question both sides openly.

sentences.zh: 若蕭復有所請求，則從一何容為隱！

translations.literal: If Xiao Fu had made some request, how could Congyi conceal it!
translations.idiomatic: If Xiao Fu had made some request, Liu Congyi could not have hidden it!

sentences.zh: 若從一自有回互，則蕭復不當受疑。

translations.literal: If Congyi himself had some evasion, then Xiao Fu ought not to be suspected.
translations.idiomatic: If Liu Congyi was the one equivocating, Xiao Fu should not be suspected.

sentences.zh: 陛下何憚而不辯明，乃直為此悵恨也！

translations.literal: Why should Your Majesty shrink from clarifying it and instead brood in regret like this!
translations.idiomatic: Why should Your Majesty shrink from clearing the matter up and instead brood over it like this!

sentences.zh: 夫明則罔惑，辨則罔冤。

translations.literal: Where there is clarity, there is no confusion; where there is examination, there is no injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Clarity dispels confusion; inquiry dispels injustice.

sentences.zh: 惑莫甚於逆詐而不與明，冤莫痛於見疑而不與辯。

translations.literal: No confusion is worse than treachery and deceit met without clarity; no injustice is more painful than being suspected without being given examination.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing breeds confusion like deceit met without clarity; nothing wounds like suspicion met without a hearing.

sentences.zh: 是使情偽相糅，忠邪靡分。

translations.literal: This makes truth and falsehood mingle together and loyalty and treachery impossible to distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: That is how truth and falsehood mingle and loyalty and treachery become impossible to tell apart.

sentences.zh: 茲實居上御下之要樞，惟陛下留意。」

translations.literal: This is truly the crucial hinge of how a ruler governs those below — may Your Majesty take it to heart."
translations.idiomatic: This is the very hinge of how a ruler governs his subjects — I urge Your Majesty to heed it."

sentences.zh: 上亦竟不復辯也。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end never examined the matter after all.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the emperor never held the inquiry at all.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以王武俊為恆、冀、深、趙節度使，壬辰，加李抱真、張孝忠並同平章事。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Wang Wujun was made military governor of Heng, Ji, Shen, and Zhao; on renchen, Li Baozhen and Zhang Xiaozhong were both given the additional title of co-director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinmao, Wang Wujun was appointed military governor of Heng, Ji, Shen, and Zhao. On renchen, Li Baozhen and Zhang Xiaozhong were both made co-directors of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丙申，加田悅檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Tian Yue was given the additional title of acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingshen, Tian Yue was appointed acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以山南東道行軍司馬樊澤為本道節度使，前深、趙觀察使康日知為同州刺史、奉誠軍節度使，曹州刺史李納為鄆州刺史、平盧節度使。

translations.literal: Fan Ze, campaign chief of staff of Shannan East Circuit, was made military governor of that circuit; Kang Rizhi, former observation commissioner of Shen and Zhao, was made prefect of Tong Prefecture and military governor of the Fengcheng Army; Li Na, prefect of Cao Prefecture, was made prefect of Yan Prefecture and military governor of Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ze, campaign chief of staff of Shannan East, became military governor of that circuit. Kang Rizhi, former observation commissioner of Shen and Zhao, became prefect of Tong and military governor of the Fengcheng Army. Li Na, prefect of Cao, became prefect of Yan and military governor of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，加劉洽汴、滑、宋、亳都統副使，知都統事，李勉悉以其眾授之。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Liu Qia was made deputy overall commander of Bian, Hua, Song, and Bo and placed in charge of overall command affairs; Li Mian turned over all his troops to him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuxu, Liu Qia was appointed deputy overall commander of Bian, Hua, Song, and Bo and given charge of overall command. Li Mian transferred all his troops to him.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，六軍各置統軍，秩從三品，以寵勳臣。

translations.literal: On xinchou, each of the Six Armies was given an army commander, rank equivalent to third grade, to honor meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinchou, each of the Six Armies received an army commander of third rank, to honor the meritorious.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃尚結贊請出兵助唐收京城。

translations.literal: Shang Jiezan of Tibet requested to send troops to help Tang recover the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Jiezan of Tibet offered to send troops to help the Tang recover the capital.

sentences.zh: 庚子，遣秘書監崔漢衡使吐蕃，發其兵。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the Director of the Palace Library Cui Hanheng was sent as envoy to Tibet to mobilize its troops.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengzi, Cui Hanheng, Director of the Palace Library, was sent as envoy to Tibet to mobilize its army.
